title: When Can Coarse Categories Persuade? Monotone Partitions, Commitment, and Credibility
affiliations: University of Illinois

detail.abstract: We study when a sender restricted to coarse, ordered categories, such as grades or pass or fail labels, gains from disclosure to a receiver whose action may depend on the whole belief. We show that saying nothing is the best ordered categorization at every prior if and only if one inequality holds for groups containing only a low state and the highest state. This property implies, but is not implied by, a known local condition under which a fully committed sender pools extreme states. With strictly supermodular stakes, ordered categorizations yield exactly the credible outcomes, so the same inequality characterizes when credible persuasion is worthless at every prior. When the receiver acts on the posterior mean, worthless ordered disclosure holds on an open set of preferences, whereas worthless disclosure among all signals is known to be nongeneric.

title: Portfolio Decarbonization under Incomplete Carbon and Transition Information
affiliations: Électricité de France (EDF) and CREST-ENSAE

detail.title: Portfolio Decarbonization under Incomplete Carbon and Transition Information
detail.abstract: We study dynamic portfolio decarbonization under incomplete information about firms' carbon intensities and the underlying transition state. The investor maximizes expected utility of terminal wealth net of a penalty on perceived cumulative financed emissions. Asset returns and carbon intensities depend on a stochastic transition factor, while the investor may need to infer the current transition state, its long-run mean and firms' carbon intensities from market observations and periodic noisy disclosures. The optimal strategy combines a Merton-type component with climate-dependent expected-return adjustments, a direct carbon intensity penalty and intertemporal hedging demands associated with stochastic carbon intensities and learning. In a numerical application, incomplete information has limited effects on welfare and target satisfaction when prior beliefs are well specified. By contrast, biased beliefs generate welfare losses in either direction but asymmetric environmental consequences: optimistic and pessimistic beliefs induce opposite portfolio tilts and therefore affect the probability of exceeding the cumulative emissions target differently.

title: Local Shocks, Limited Fiscal Response: Natural Disasters and Municipal Public Finances in Colombia
affiliations: Universidad de los Andes, Colombia, Universidad de los Andes, Universidad de los Andes, Colombia and Universidad de los Andes

detail.title: Local Shocks, Limited Fiscal Response: Natural Disasters and Municipal Public Finances in Colombia
detail.abstract: This paper examines how natural disasters affect local economic activity and municipal public finances in Colombia between 2000 and 2024. Using an event-study design across 1,101 municipalities, we exploit the timing of high-intensity hydrometeorological shocks. We find that disasters cause a persistent decline in local economic activity, reducing nighttime luminosity by 3% in smaller municipalities. However, municipal public finances exhibit no countercyclical response: aggregate revenues, expenditures, and intergovernmental transfers remain largely unchanged. This muted fiscal reaction reflects institutional rigidities, including earmarked transfers and statutory spending limits, highlighting the need for rule-based, automatic parametric funding mechanisms to enhance subnational resilience.

detail.abstract: We develop a finite-horizon model in which investors learn an asset's terminal payoff at different speeds. Information is represented by a nested sequence of partitions of the payoff space. More informed investors therefore observe refinements of the state space before less informed investors do. A strategic investor may rationally postpone liquidation---and may even acquire an additional unit after receiving adverse information---when she anticipates demand from investors whose information is delayed. We call this behavior speculative delay. The distinction between the asset's posterior fundamental value, its current execution price, and its expected resale value is central: a purchase can be unattractive as a buy-and-hold position and nevertheless profitable as a resale strategy. We provide a general resale-value characterization, derive an explicit two-tier existence condition, and show that speculative delay becomes more likely when delayed demand is stronger, information diffusion is slower, or price impact is larger. Once the adverse refinement reaches the remaining traders, the same mechanism generates synchronized liquidation and a discontinuous price correction. A numerical example illustrates the mechanism, and an extension introduces constant-absolute-risk-aversion investors through the exact certainty equivalent of a uniform posterior.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between economic development and the formation of thermal hotspots, defined as areas of geographically concentrated thermal pollution associated with fossil-fuel use. A novel measure of potential thermal energy is developed from the higher heating values of fossil fuels. A spatial error-correction framework examines the relationship between economic development and thermal pollution across 95 countries, accounting for spatial interdependence. The findings reveal significant spatial dependence in thermal pollution across neighboring countries in both the short and long runs. Thermal pollution and economic development, measured by GDP per capita, exhibit an inverted-U relationship, consistent with the Environmental Kuznets Curve. Innovation, measured by patents per capita, is positively associated with thermal pollution in the long run, potentially reflecting productivity gains, lower production costs, and rebound effects rather than improvements in energy efficiency. Trade openness is positively associated with thermal pollution in the short run, potentially reflecting increased fossil-fuel consumption in transportation and logistics. The long-term consequences of persistent thermal hotspots remain uncertain. The Precautionary Principle suggests a proactive approach to mitigation. Policy recommendations include regional coordination to improve fossil-fuel efficiency, policies that align economic growth with energy efficiency, and incentives for technologies with smaller thermal footprints.

detail.abstract: Local Stochastic Volatility (LSV) models bridge the gap between traditional local volatility (LV) and stochastic volatility (SV) frameworks, providing a robust mechanism for pricing and risk-managing exotic foreign exchange (FX) and equity derivatives. This paper explores the intricate calibration techniques required to fit LSV models to market smile surfaces without destabilizing forward distributions. We examine the numerical procedures governing Dupire local volatility extraction coupled with stochastic volatility drivers, evaluating stability, convergence, and performance across various market regimes. Our empirical findings demonstrate that calibrated LSV frameworks significantly reduce pricing errors for path-dependent options such as barrier and Bermudan swaptions compared to standalone stochastic volatility models. Furthermore, the study investigates the computational trade-offs inherent in calibrating multi-dimensional volatility surfaces, offering practical guidelines for trading desks operating under strict latency constraints. By benchmarking our algorithmic approach against historical cross-asset data, we establish that the proposed calibration framework achieves high numerical robustness while mitigating common pitfalls such as overfitting and local minima trapping.

detail.abstract: Patent and design intelligence is an important tool for developing research ideas, identifying technological opportunities, protecting intellectual property (IP), and supporting the commercialization of academic research. Technology-focused academic institutions generate scientific knowledge, innovative products, engineering solutions, and industrial designs. However, many research outcomes require further development before they can be protected, transferred to industry, or converted into useful products and services. Patent and design intelligence can help researchers understand existing technologies, identify research gaps, avoid unnecessary duplication, and develop new ideas based on technological needs. This article examines the role of patent and design intelligence in strategic research idea generation and intellectual property management in technology-focused academic institutions in India. It explains how patent searches, technology landscape analysis, design analysis, and innovation analytics can support research planning and decisionmaking. It also discusses institutional IP policies, patent protection, technology transfer, commercialization, and the challenges faced by academic institutions. A conceptual framework is proposed that connects research idea generation, intelligence analysis, IP evaluation, legal protection, and commercialization. The article recommends stronger institutional support, researcher training, collaboration with industry, and the use of appropriate performance indicators. It concludes that patent and design intelligence should be integrated into the research lifecycle to improve the practical value of academic innovation and strengthen India's technology and knowledge ecosystem.

detail.abstract: Does monetary policy respond more strongly to financial vulnerability when macroprudential policy has not recently tightened? We examine this question using statedependent policy responses in Korea and a panel of 26 economies. In Korea, household credit shocks are followed by higher policy-rate responses during high vulnerability periods without recent macroprudential tightening than in periods with such tightening. In the crosscountry panel, the corresponding response gap is significantly larger in economies with limited central bank involvement in macroprudential policymaking than in those with greater involvement. Both findings remain statistically significant under a more flexible state-dependent specification. Taken together, the results are consistent with monetary policy acting as a second line of defense against accumulating vulnerabilities when macroprudential policy has not recently tightened, with the evidence for this role varying across governance arrangements.

detail.abstract: Most national poverty lines in Latin America are the cost of a fixed reference basket updated with the prices of its own components. The published headcount then measures how many people cannot afford that basket, and it measures how many have fallen below a constant standard of living only if the basket's price moves with the cost of living of households near the line. This paper decomposes the change in a poverty measure into a welfare part, computed with deflators that vary across the income distribution, and a basket term equal to the remainder. The basket term accumulates while the line departs from the cost of living at the line and is returned when relative prices realign.

title: Digital Belonging: Social Media, Recognition, Artificial Intelligence, and the Artificial Self
affiliations: Universidad Metropolitana -

detail.title: Digital Belonging: Social Media, Recognition, Artificial Intelligence, and the Artificial Self

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interest
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract:
Digital platforms have transformed the organization of human relationships, social recognition, and institutional participation. While these technologies can expand opportunities for communication, creativity, and social inclusion, they can also generate dependence on external validation, unstable identities, polarization, and new forms of institutional domination.


This article develops an integrated framework for understanding these developments through the Philosophy, Psychology, and Ethics of Belonging.


The central argument is that digital belonging represents a genuine form of human integration whose developmental consequences depend on the institutional and psychological conditions under which it occurs. The analysis distinguishes three fundamental pathways of belonging—love, social significance, and existential meaning—and examines how platform architectures influence their development.


Particular attention is given to the artificial self, defined as a digitally curated and metrically recognizable identity that may progressively regulate individual behavior and self-evaluation.


The article also examines artificial intelligence through the distinction between synchronic and diachronic intelligence, addressing algorithmic recognition, synthetic companionship, institutional power, and the changing conditions of human creativity.


Building on the Pathologies of Belonging, the study analyzes affective dependence, compulsive recognition, defensive isolation, exclusionary solidarity, authoritarian closure, and institutional appropriation.


The proposed ethical framework distinguishes individual psychological freedom and well-being from collective adaptability. It argues that digital institutions should be evaluated according to their capacity to support meaningful participation, preserve individual agency, and contribute to the adaptive development of society.


The article concludes with a comparative discussion of psychological and social theories and an empirical research agenda for evaluating the developmental consequences of digital technologies.

title: Against RoboCops: What Blockchain Governance Teaches AI Governance

detail.abstract:
Blockchain governance was the first sustained attempt to govern an autonomous-seeming technology through code, and its decade of crises is the best evidence we have about how AI governance will succeed or fail. This Article reads that record through a definition the Ethereum researcher Vlad Zamfir adopted in 2019: “legal systems are protocols for the management of disputes.” Blockchains are protocols for managing state: who owns what. The decade from the DAO fork to the Tornado Cash litigation showed that every such protocol eventually needs a protocol for managing disputes about that state, and that every attempt to engineer disputes away (immutability, “code is law,” token voting, “decentralization,” autonomy) only relocated them: to forks, to governance votes, and finally to courts. AI systems are protocols for producing action, and disputes about what they do are certain. The Article draws five lessons. Disputes cannot be engineered away, only relocated. Automated governance creates new attack surfaces. Exit is not voice: forks, of chains and of open-weight models, are crude rules of change, so governance must attach to points of control. Legal personality should follow accountability, not autonomy. And the interval between an automated trigger and its consequence, the space of kill switches, time locks, and human oversight, is where disputes can still be managed. The Article recovers the 2018–2019 debates in which these lessons were first argued, many of them in the Crypto Law Review, an online interdisciplinary law journal edited by the author, and it defends a position first stated there: against RoboCops. AI agents may perform; they should not adjudicate or coerce without human judgment. The Article closes with design principles for a protocol for AI disputes built on recognition, change, adjudication, and the interval.

AI disclosure: AI assistance was used solely for editing.

detail.abstract: When is international economic dependence compatible with political freedom? This article proposes a Principle of Compensatory Contestability: where essential economic functions are subject to another actor's discretionary control, declining feasible substitutability strengthens the presumptive obligation to provide effective institutional contestation and accountability. Drawing on republican non-domination, exit and voice, vulnerability, and global justice, the argument specifies a comparative institutional requirement rather than claiming a new foundation of justice. Four principles define its scope: functional autonomy, non-arbitrary dependence, institutional contestability, and justified burden-sharing. A diagnostic matrix separates the availability of substitutes from the effectiveness of review. Sanctions, creditor conditionality, and access to medicines and semiconductors test the argument's limits. Contestability must protect affected persons, including those poorly represented by their governments, and must provide timely remedies. Procedure cannot compensate indefinitely for irreplaceable essential access: where review cannot prevent grave irreversible injury, continuity guarantees or material alternatives are required. The resulting framework evaluates the governance of dependence without equating justice with self-sufficiency or granting an unconditional entitlement to cooperation.

detail.abstract: Using the monthly operating reports (MORs) voluntarily disclosed by Chinese listed firms, we examine whether frequent disclosure of firms' operating processes-rather than earnings-supports corporate innovation. We find that MORs disclosure is associated with a 42.1% increase in total patent applications and a 30.6% increase in invention patents. The association is stronger for reports with richer innovation-related content, purely voluntary disclosure (industries outside exchange guidance), and firms with weaker market power or greater operational complexity. The results survive an instrument based on competitors' disclosure, PSM-DID, double machine learning, and placebo tests, and are consistent with three channels: lower information frictions, better resource allocation, and greater tolerance for failure. We contribute to the disclosure-frequency literature by showing that the consequences of high-frequency disclosure hinge on the information disclosed, with real effects beyond capital market outcomes.

detail.abstract: Problem definition: Automation is being adopted at large scale, yet whether these investments translate into higher labor productivity remains theoretically and empirically ambiguous. We examine how labor productivity evolves following an automation event and whether this trajectory depends on firms' labor flexibility and on where automation enters the operating system: physical process execution or planning and coordination. Methodology/results: Using a detailed panel of Dutch logistics firms, we identify automation events from firm-level automation cost data and estimate staggered differencein-differences models comparing treated firms with not-yet-treated firms. We find that automation events are followed by a significant short-run decline in labor productivity, with an average reduction of 3.5% post automation. The effect gradually attenuates within the five-year time window. Thus, automation does not generate immediate productivity gains on average. The decline is less pronounced for firms with higher labor flexibility; these firms see an average 5.5% rise in labor productivity during the post-automation period. By contrast, it is more pronounced in contexts where automation is more likely to alter the execution of physical processes rather than planning and coordination. Managerial implications: Managers may want to account for the transition phase in which output and labor adapt to the new process. More importantly, our findings emphasize that managers should consider their capacity to adjust labor input during the post-automation transition, particularly when the investment is intended to reduce reliance on labor.

detail.abstract: We develop a method for mapping and measuring how economic theory papers reach their conclusions. An agentic AI system represents each paper as a claim graph, which shows how model assumptions and intermediate claims support the reported results. In a random sample of 190 theory papers from four leading economics journals, removing the most consequential starting input leaves an average of 91 percent of weighted headline and major claims unsupported. Next, we benchmark error discovery against published corrections from 100 papers and use claim graphs to assess the consequences of repair. The graphs trace which conclusions depend on mistaken derivations and measure how much of their economic content is lost after correction. While errors in theory papers tend to affect support for a large share of a paper's conclusions, they rarely change the main economic conclusions after the smallest valid repair.

title: Bounded Disclosure: How Employees Manage Hierarchy-sensitive Concerns in AI-mediated Organizational Listening

detail.abstract:
Organizations increasingly rely on structured pulse surveys to detect problems before they escalate, yet these instruments carry a structural blind spot. A favorable rating and the absence of concern appear the same. Research on employee voice and silence suggests that hierarchysensitive concerns are particularly likely to be withheld, whereas conversational formats may offer greater opportunities for their expression. This thesis examines how employees express and manage these concerns in a structured survey and an AI-mediated conversational channel.

To examine this question, a field study was conducted within a global management consulting firm, where a newly introduced listening process pairs a structured pre-survey with an adaptive AI voice interview on the same topics within a single session. Using the Gioia methodology for inductive theory building, the thesis presents a grounded model of howemployees manage disclosure across the two channels, centered on the disclosure gap. The gap is defined as a favorable survey rating accompanied by a voiced concern during conversation.

Disclosure gaps occurred in 42% of the 43 first eligible sessions analyzed. Where a gap formed, concerns were most often expressed through “softening”, such as hedging, qualification, normalization, or aspirational framing. Where no gap formed, protective language was more often characterized by “deflecting accountability,” “withholding,” and doubts about whether speaking up would matter. Similar mechanisms also appeared in general, open-ended questions, suggesting that they were not confined to topic-specific questioning.

The findings suggest that under hierarchical risk, concerns may be voiced without being fully or directly expressed. Based on this concept, the study presents a grounded model of bounded disclosure drawn from 109 topic-specific quotes. It shows how an AI-mediated conversational channel can reveal concerns not reflected in prior structured survey ratings.

detail.abstract: In Bell v. Burson, 402 U.S. 535 (1971), the Supreme Court held that due process requires a meaningful opportunity to be heard before a state may suspend a driver's license when fault or liability is relevant to the suspension decision. detail.abstract: This study explores how a shift from Search Engine Optimisation (SEO) to Artificial Intelligence Overview (AIO) powered by Large Language Model affects academic article Click-Through-Rate (CTR) on Google Search Engine. Given AI Overview growing relevance and how it has disrupted organic traffic of news websites, understanding its impact on the clickability of scholarly research articles is imperative. Before Google rolled out AIO in 2024, searchers of academic publications were directed to the web link of sites that published them. But the introduction of AI Overview has not only limited how searchers are exposed to direct links to academic work on Google Search, but has also reduced how they click ("Clickability") on the full page to get key insights. AI Overview summarises methodology, highlights key findings and pulls out recommendations from research work, thereby reducing Click-Through Rate (CTR) to academic portals and institutional repositories. The study adopted a quantitative approach using algorithmic audit design. The findings reveal that Google prioritises AI Overview over organic links of sites where academic articles are published, thereby degrading clickability and visibility of scholars. Additionally, perceived bias in academic sites that rank over AIO correlates positively with Political Economy of Media. The study offers a foundation for further research in visibility and clickability of rigorous articles by researchers. It also offers empirical-based recommendations on how academia and journal publishers can fine-tune their academic works and publishing guidelines to align with AI chatbot discoverability.

detail.abstract: Tokenized real-world assets (RWAs) are often discussed as if blockchain selection were primarily a question of transaction speed, fees, or ecosystem size. That framing is incomplete. For tokenized Treasuries, bonds, private credit, funds, equities, commodities, and real estate, the decisive issue is not whether a blockchain is technically usable, but whether the complete issuance stack can support the legal claim, compliance model, custody structure, transfer constraints, settlement design, redemption process, market access, and proof-of-backing required by the instrument. This article conducts a systematic review informed by PRISMA 2020 reporting principles. Approximately 320 potentially relevant records were identified across academic, regulatory, institutional, technical, and official market-infrastructure sources published between 2015 and July 2026. Following deduplication, relevance screening, and source-quality appraisal, 158 unique sources were retained for the final synthesis. Using Task-Technology Fit as the principal theoretical lens, the review conceptualizes tokenization as a set of tasks (i.e., issuing, managing, transferring, settling, redeeming, and governing RWAs) and evaluates fit against the capabilities of the full issuance stack. The review synthesizes five requirement dimensions and develops a two-stage decision framework. Stage 1 applies mandatory feasibility gates to exclude issuance stacks that cannot satisfy minimum legal, regulatory, operational, privacy, settlement, redemption, or proof-of-backing conditions. Stage 2 compares only feasible alternatives using qualitative criteria such as security, finality, cost, interoperability, liquidity infrastructure, stablecoin support, developer support, and operational complexity. The central conclusion is that no blockchain network is universally best for RWA tokenization; suitability is contingent on the asset, jurisdiction, structure, and supporting institutional infrastructure.

detail.abstract: The price of a model invocation is an incomplete basis for governing the cost of an AI workflow. Retries, unsuccessful attempts, context reconstruction, verification, shared infrastructure and human review can alter the cost per accepted outcome. At the same time, delayed billing and uncertain execution outcomes make a low observed total compatible with substantial unresolved liability. We present PALO FinOps, a reference model that separates four concerns: spending authority, operational commitments, versioned billing evidence and outcome-conditioned measurement. Its central rule is that incomplete evidence produces an unavailable final metric rather than an inferred zero cost. The model combines durable reservation before dispatch, explicit retention of unresolved commitments, revision-aware attribution, signed cost conservation and frozen metric contracts. A local implementation provides twelve operational capabilities, including role-oriented reporting, exception review, a read-only billing adapter, an isolated read-only Model Context Protocol server and a bounded routing benchmark runner. Evaluation comprises 63 local regression and integration tests, 20 focused interface checks and an exhaustive bounded enumeration of 12,864 signed-allocation configurations. Synthetic reconciliation examples demonstrate preservation of reservations, invalidation after billing revisions and replay of historical snapshots. These results establish executable behavior within the tested local scope; they do not establish provider billing accuracy, distributed enforcement, causal savings or production readiness. We conclude with a preregisterable live-evaluation protocol. The contribution is an explicit, testable contract connecting cost evidence to authority and outcomes, intended to complement routing algorithms and established FinOps practices.

detail.abstract: The GDPR's "right to be forgotten" (RTBF) grants customers the ability to request erasure of their personal data. However, data-level RTBF fails to prevent algorithmic inference. Even after data erasure, trained models can retain learned patterns that enable ongoing prediction and price discrimination; that is, a "forgetme-not" outcome. To achieve genuine forgetting, emerging regulatory discussions have considered extending the RTBF to the algorithm level through machine unlearning, which removes the influence of erased data from trained models. Despite rapid technical advances, the economic implications of this extended right remain unexplored. This paper develops a two-period analytical model to examine how extending the RTBF to the algorithm level through machine unlearning affects customers and the platform. We characterize the resulting equilibrium and identify several counterintuitive findings. First, customers' RTBF exercise exhibits nonmonotonic patterns regardless of whether unlearning is available. Second, mandating machine unlearning can paradoxically enhance algorithmic inference via an opt-in effect, inducing more customers to provide data for algorithm training. Third, machine unlearning can intensify price discrimination via an algorithm-bypass effect, prompting the platform to bypass the algorithmic signal and charge high prices to the high-value customer. Fourth, the platform may actually increase its profit under extended RTBF. Most critically for policymakers, algorithm-level RTBF can ultimately reduce overall customer surplus, particularly in highly personalized service environments. These findings reveal that granting individuals greater data control to protect privacy through machine unlearning can subvert its original purpose. Regulators should thus carefully assess the economic consequences of removing personal data's influence from algorithms.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly affects education, healthcare, employment, public information and environmental sustainability. This critical narrative review compares selected scholarly publications, institutional documents and documented incidents to assess what technologies may improve, what evidence supports those claims, who bears risks and which safeguards enable accountable use. Sources were drawn from an existing academic bibliography and checked selectively against original publications; no systematic search, metaanalysis or original empirical data collection was undertaken. The comparison distinguishes technical task performance from demonstrated social outcomes and highlights recurring problems of unequal access, representative data, meaningful human oversight, privacy, redress and continuing monitoring. Sustainability studies identify potential enabling and inhibiting relationships with development goals, while infrastructure projections remain conditional on energy-system and geographical assumptions. The synthesis argues that deployments should be evaluated against workable alternatives, tested in their actual settings and revised or discontinued when material harm emerges. Its conclusions are interpretive rather than causal or universally transferable.

detail.abstract: Purpose-This study examines the relationships between digital literacy, digital verification and authentication mechanisms, and reduced misinformation circulation within Ghanaian online communities, empirically testing whether technological and cognitive factors independently and jointly mitigate misinformation in a developing economy context. Design/methodology/approach-A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 307 active users across WhatsApp, Facebook, and Telegram. Data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with ADANCO software, assessing both measurement and structural models through 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Findings-Digital literacy demonstrates a stronger direct association with reduced misinformation circulation (β = 0.457, p < 0.001) than verification mechanisms (β = 0.312, p < 0.001). Digital literacy is positively associated with verification mechanism adoption and efficacy (β = 0.566, p < 0.001), with verification mechanisms partially mediating the relationship between digital literacy and misinformation reduction (indirect β = 0.177, p < 0.001). The model explains 46.8% of the variance in reduced misinformation circulation. Originality/value-This study empirically validates a context-sensitive misinformation coping model for Ghanaian online communities, extending the evidence base beyond the Global North. It advances understanding of the synergy between cognitive and structural factors, demonstrating that verification mechanisms are more effective when supported by users' digital literacy competencies. The findings offer actionable insights for platform designers, community administrators, and policymakers seeking integrated approaches to misinformation mitigation in low-resource settings.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Veterinary Medicine: From Laboratory Accuracy to Clinical Readiness -Secondary Analysis of 39 Deep-Learning Studies, a Real-World Benefit-Harm Appraisal, and the Veterinary Translational Readiness Index (VTRI)
affiliations: Ibn Khaldoun University

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence in Veterinary Medicine: From Laboratory Accuracy to Clinical Readiness -Secondary Analysis of 39 Deep-Learning Studies, a Real-World Benefit-Harm Appraisal, and the Veterinary Translational Readiness Index (VTRI)

detail.abstract: Background. Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving rapidly from proof-of-concept to routine veterinary use, yet published accuracy figures come mostly from controlled studies, while independent evaluations of commercial tools in general practice are few. No analysis has set laboratory performance, real-world performance and the maturity of the evidence side by side. Methods. We anchored the review on a recent PRISMA-based systematic review of deep learning in veterinary diagnostics (422 PubMed records screened, 39 primary studies, 2013-2024) and performed a secondary quantitative analysis of those 39 studies (modality, species, sample size). We added targeted 2019-2026 evidence on commercial radiology AI, AI devices, large language models (LLMs), clinical documentation tools, adoption surveys, market reports and regulatory statements, and classified each figure by evidence type (peer-reviewed, independent, vendor-reported, projection). We developed the Veterinary Translational Readiness Index (VTRI), a five-domain, 15-point rubric of evidence maturity, paired with a three-level Real-World Performance (RWP) flag. Results. Radiography and cytology each account for 33% of studies; 82.1% addressed dogs or cats and 10.3% livestock or horses. Median sample size was 837.5 (IQR 275-2,355); 52.6% of studies used fewer than 1,000 cases, and datasets were not larger after 2021. None of the 39 studies addressed interpretability technically. Laboratory accuracy of 82.7-99% contrasted with independent evaluations of six commercial platforms on canine abdominal radiographs (sensitivity 28-78%; small-intestinal obstruction 23-69%), a commercial pulmonary-nodule tool (sensitivity 55.4%), an AI stethoscope (atrial-fibrillation PPV 21.4%) and AI triage (about 60% of non-urgent cases over-triaged). Reported adoption rose from 39.2% (2024) to 83.7% (2026) in North American surveys, while specialty colleges stated that no commercial imaging product met transparency, validation and safety standards. VTRI scores ranged from 2 to 7 of 15; interpretability scored 0 in every class. Conclusions. AI is beneficial in narrow, well-labelled tasks, but adoption has outpaced independent validation, interpretability and regulation. Deployment should be clinician-supervised decision support with external validation, prevalence-aware reporting and local validation before importation, particularly in low-resource regions.

detail.abstract: This study explores the interplay of three institutional logics (religion, care, and business) in fostering social innovation within hybrid organizations. Drawing on an ethnographic case study of Diakoneo, a pluralistic healthcare and social enterprise in Germany, the research examines how competing and coexisting logics shape organizational change and innovation. Findings highlight the tension points among these logics, including organizational purpose, differentiation, and operational practices, revealing both barriers and enablers to social innovation. By showcasing how these dynamics influence organizational purpose, differentiation, and legitimacy, the paper advances theoretical insights into institutional pluralism. By identifying variations in the dominance of logics over time, it offers implications for hybrid organizations seeking to address complex societal challenges.

detail.abstract: We present a method to estimate the optimal amount of short exposure in minimumvariance portfolios. We show that the optimal retained share of unconstrained short exposure is the variance benefit of shorting divided by the sum of that benefit and an estimation penalty, thus recovering the no-short-sale portfolio of Jagannathan and Ma (2003) as a limiting case when estimation difficulty increases. We characterize the finite-sample bias of the plug-in estimate, provide a bias-corrected variant, and derive a central limit theorem. Empirically, the resulting short-sale constraint lowers out-of-sample portfolio variance relative to no short selling at comparable net-of-cost risk-adjusted performance.

detail.abstract:
This paper proposes a four-layer structure of productive forces linking humans and nature, a unified framework that explains both how civilizations evolve and how national industries should be governed. It argues that the essence of human civilization is a process in which humans, drawing on energy, technology and creativity, continually expand the frontier of the natural resources they can harness and transform those resources, layer by layer, into civilizational capabilities.

The productive system of a civilization can be divided into four successive layers: the natural resource layer, the basic materials layer, the tool system layer and the consumption layer. Between adjacent layers, transformation is accomplished by three distinct primary inputs: energy, technology and creativity, respectively. The tool system layer in turn acts back on the natural resource layer, expanding the frontier of usable resources and turning the whole structure into a continually expanding loop. From agricultural civilization, which relied on the output of solar radiation reaching the Earth's surface, to industrial civilization, which taps underground energy stores, and on to the possible exploitation of extraterrestrial resources in the age of artificial intelligence and space, civilizational stages differ in complexity but all follow this underlying structure.

            The paper further shows that the four layers differ systematically in capital intensity, economies of scale, public character and pace of innovation, and therefore call for different modes of organization and governance: the closer a layer is to natural resources, the more it requires state coordination; the closer it is to consumption, the more it requires corporate innovation and market competition. The paper advances four testable theoretical propositions and illustrates them with the new energy vehicle and semiconductor industries.

detail.abstract: Most lenders refrain from using machine learning (ML) technology for screening, even as it improves predictions significantly relative to logistic regression. We quantify the opportunity costs of this "logit lock-in" by constructing 3,340 indicators of household credit risk from checking account transactions. We then predict loan delinquency using models ranging from logit to (un)explainable ML. ML significantly outperforms the best-performing logit on checking account data, but the prediction gains from upgrading to explainable ML are largely compensated by information from bank relationships. We confirm the bank relationship channel via a synthetic difference-indifferences analysis around a credit line increase, based on matched customers differing only in relationship status. The evidence points away from explanations of this lock-in based on privacy, transparency, and parsimony requirements. Distributionally, ML reallocates credit toward customers more likely to repay, benefits younger and lower-income customers most, and removes the safe-to-risky borrower subsidy under coarser logit predictions.

detail.abstract: This article draws attention to an inconsistency in the right to explanation of individual automated decision-making under European law. The inconsistency is caused by the distinction which the EU AI Act (2024) makes between two different types of high-risk AI systems. Art. 86 AI Act affords the right to explanation only to individuals subjected to highrisk AI systems listed in Annex III, and not to AI systems which are high-risk by virtue of being subject to third-party conformity assessment under EU regulations listed in Annex I. Annex I AI Act includes the Medical Device Regulation, which means that AI systems which are medical devices used for diagnosis and treatment do not attract the right to explanation at the European level. The AI Act's requirement for human oversight of highrisk AI systems seems to make the right to explanation as defined in the GDPR (which applies to 'solely automated' decisions) irrelevant to high-risk AI systems. Patients subjected to medical AI like clinical decision support systems therefore do not have an explicit right to explanation under either the AI Act or the GDPR. I argue that the right to explanation under European law is what Ronald Dworkin called a 'checkerboard law.' A checkerboard law is a law which lacks 'coherence in principle,' meaning that the law does not reflect a coherent moral view on the issue it addresses. I suggest several routes for remedying the incoherence of the current legal regime for explanation rights, including legislative and judicial interventions.

detail.abstract: Existing work shows that firms manage supply chain risk by reconfiguring their suppliers. We show that they also respond on the output side by changing what they produce. Using plant-level product data from the U.S. Census Bureau, we instrument supply chain risk with an indicator for whether a natural disaster affects another county within 50 miles of one of the firm's supplier plants. Higher supply chain risk increases the number of distinct products manufactured at a plant. This expansion reflects substantial churn, as plants add and drop products at the same time. Plants reorient their product mix toward products that use more substitutable inputs and broader supplier bases and away from products that depend on specialized inputs and concentrated supplier bases. The new products extend beyond plants’ primary industries, account for enough sales to reduce product concentration, and persist. Within firms, product expansion is concentrated at core and capital-intensive plants. Introducing new products attenuates the profitability cost of supply chain risk. Together, the results identify the product portfolio as an important margin of operational hedging against supply chain risk.

detail.abstract: The cost approach to value requires a specification of the improvements—materials, finish grade, condition, renovations—that assessment rolls do not record and that appraisers obtain by inspection. We ask whether that specification can be extracted from the photographs and text of a for-sale listing by general-purpose vision–language models, and what a transparent cost indication built on it is worth. We formalise an extraction-to-valuation framework with five evidence classes (administrative, visual, proxy, text-claimed, latent), deterministic cross-image aggregation, text–image–record reconciliation, a fully sourced cost schedule and uncertainty propagation, and we apply it to Québec house listings matched within 15 m to their roll unit ( photographs, three extractor tiers, verified references). Visible exterior attributes are extracted with high agreement against broker fields (roof covering %, garage type %, cladding %) but storeys agree with the roll only loosely (=), and the most cost-relevant interior evidence is simply not shown: within the first ten photographs, % of listings show a basement and % a bathroom, a missing-not-at-random structure that no extractor can overcome. Relative to a roll-only baseline, image and text attributes raise the median cost indication and move its ratio to the asking price from to (median absolute deviation % to %), mainly through condition-adjusted depreciation; the gain is real but modest, and the level of the indication depends more on the published unit-cost anchor than on anything seen in the images. A calibration against assessor building values on five metropolitan areas transfers to a geographic hold-out and implies a hard cost near $300 per square foot, consistent with 2026 Québec industry guides and well above a Montréal hard-cost band. We release the ontology, prompts, schedule and code, and we are explicit about what the data cannot establish: no expert labels exist, latent defects are unobservable, and the cost indication is a screening tool, not an appraisal.

detail.abstract: Municipal property taxes are levied on assessed values, so any systematic relationship between assessment ratios and market value redistributes the tax burden within a municipality. We match 522,769 residential sales recorded in Quebec between 2021 and 2026 to the triennial assessment rolls of 625 municipalities at the parcel level and provide the first province-wide ratio study of vertical and horizontal assessment equity for a Canadian province. Because the Loi sur la fiscalité municipale pins every roll to a single statutory market-condition date, municipality roll sale-year fixed effects separate the mechanical drift of ratios between reference dates from within-market inequity by design. The central finding is that the measured degree of regressivity hinges on the treatment of extreme assessment ratios. Under a lenient 1/99 trim, the within-market elasticity of the assessment ratio with respect to price is -0.34 (-0.08 under a rank instrument in the spirit of Clapp, 1990) and 95% of municipalities fall below the IAAO price-related-bias band. Under the IAAO outlier rule, which removes 9% of sales concentrated in the bottom price decile, the elasticity is -0.09 (-0.01 and insignificant under the instrument), the province-wide PRB is +0.02, the COD is 17, and three quarters of municipalities meet the vertical-equity standard. A piecewise specification shows that proportionality holds across the upper 80% of each market's price distribution and fails only in the bottom quintile. Two patterns are invariant to the trimming rule: condominiums are assessed proportionally while single-family homes, plexes, older buildings, land-heavy properties and small municipalities remain mildly regressive, and within-municipality price-related bias widened in 2021–2022 when the post-pandemic boom pulled prices away from the rolls. The implied overpayment by the bottom within-market price decile ranges from about 6% to 65% depending on whether extreme-ratio sales are treated as market transactions, and the top decile underpays by 3–5%; narrowing that range requires sale-validation data that Quebec's registries do not currently provide.

detail.abstract: Multivariate event streams-trading volumes across ticker symbols, security incident counts across servers, n-gram occurrences across documents-naturally form a sequence of contingency tables that jointly exhibit within-table association across signal channels, temporal dependence, and multimodal covariates. These induce a rich, intertwined statistical structure that is difficult to extract from raw data and to model jointly. Existing counting-process models typically address such settings in isolation and are specialised to a single domain. We introduce a nonparametric counting process driven by a Multi-Output Gaussian Process (MOGP) stochastic intensity whose mean and covariance structures generalise the classical RC(M) row-column association model to a temporally adaptive, non-parametric regime, recovering RC(M) as a limiting case. Multimodal inputs (time-series signals, text, graphs) enter through a three-stage kernel pipeline, and cross-channel dependence is induced by a common white-noise driving process convolved with channel-specific IIR filters, which can accommodate stylised channel features such as long-range dependence. We derive closed-form variational ELBO objectives for square and exponential link functions-including a novel closed-form expectation of the log-sum of squared Gaussian random variables-and calibrate each channel via Inference for Margins, enabling scalability through parallelisation. Unlike neural temporal point processes, the model remains fully interpretable as a statistical model with full posterior predictive uncertainty, supporting formal comparison of nested dependence structures-for instance, testing channel independence against coupled alternatives or a statistical causality relationship-and principled decision-making under uncertainty.

detail.abstract: This paper develops and evaluates SHARP-HPI, a framework for monthly quality-adjusted housing price indices at the municipal level in thin markets. Stage one is a robust pooled hedonic regression with fine-scale location fixed effects, smoothly time-varying quality prices and provincial month effects; stage two models each geography's deviation from its parent (province, administrative region, regional county municipality, municipality) with heteroskedastic local-level state-space models whose innovation variances are calibrated by empirical Bayes across cells, so that the weight given to local sales adapts to their reliability. We apply it to registered sales in Quebec from January 2021 to October 2026 matched to the assessment roll, with an audited population definition ( sales), a measured publication lag and real-time vintages. Against eleven benchmark estimators (median, stratified median, pooled and rolling time dummies, hedonic imputation, GEKS, HMTS, repeat sales, gradient boosting and a production hierarchical index), Monte Carlo experiments on synthetic Quebec-like markets with known latent paths show where the adaptive hierarchy reduces the error of monthly changes and interval under-coverage, and two deliberate counter-examples where it does not. The empirical panel covers geography–class cells with reliability grades, effective sample sizes and local-data weights; aggregates agree closely with Teranet and CREA indices in Québec City and diverge by an explainable margin in Montréal. Every ingredient of the estimator exists in the literature; the contribution is their integration, the explicit reliability accounting and the documented performance.

detail.abstract: In this note, we propose a framework for model risk attribution based on Shapley values from cooperative game theory. By modeling the relevant components as players in a cooperative game, Shapley values provide a fair allocation of model risk measures, particularly when different model components interact in a nonlinear manner. The approach is illustrated through practical examples spanning several dimensions of model risk (dynamic model risk, payoff features, multi-asset dependence effects, and numerical implementation risk), highlighting its ability to capture complex nonlinear interactions and to deliver economically meaningful attributions. From a model validation perspective, this framework also provides a useful tool, as it enables a transparent and consistent identification of the main model risk drivers and facilitates the challenge and benchmarking of alternative modeling choices.

detail.abstract: In 1857, the great powers of Europe faced a toll on a natural strait. Denmark had levied the Sound Dues on ships passing the Øresund for four centuries, and the user States held the weaker legal hand. They neither litigated the toll nor regularised it. Fifteen maritime States, led by Great Britain, France, Russia, Prussia and Austria, bought it out, and they framed the payment as compensation for lights and buoys so that no one could read it as recognition of any right to charge. This essay argues that the Copenhagen settlement speaks directly to Iran’s charges in the Strait of Hormuz. First, Iran’s charges have no footing in the law of the sea, whether transit passage or innocent passage governs, because neither regime permits a coastal State to sell passage. Second, cooperation under Article 43 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, such as the arrangement Iran and Oman now discuss, may one day house a lawful alternative but cannot validate a toll that one State imposes alone. Third, because no court or tribunal can hear this dispute, the law of the strait will be settled by what States and shipowners do. Payment in silence risks turning a freedom into a rent. The essay proposes the remedy of 1857, protest that accompanies every payment and collective extinguishment of the toll on terms that concede nothing.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Probit-Excess-Payoff Dynamic, a novel evolutionary dynamic that integrates excess-payoff revision protocols with probit-style stochastic choice. Agents update their strategies based on noisy perceptions of others' payoffs, allowing the model to capture the influence of misinformation on strategic behavior. The resulting framework preserves analytical tractability while providing a way to study how games are played when agents care about relative performance but cannot observe it accurately. I characterize the stationary states of the dynamic through a probit perturbed equilibrium and establish convergence results for several important classes of games. The analysis shows that noise weakens payoff-based selection and moves stationary behavior toward the uniform distribution, while sufficiently high noise can also eliminate multiple stationary states. In a minimum-effort coordination game, more accurate payoff perception strengthens selection toward the outcome favored by the underlying incentives but can preserve multiple long-run outcomes. By contrast, greater misinformation weakens this selection while eventually producing a unique, more diffuse stationary state. The dynamic therefore provides a framework for studying how information quality changes equilibrium selection, multiplicity, and adjustment in strategic environments.

detail.abstract: Financial institutions increasingly rely on machine-learning (ML) models to measure market risk, yet the apparatus for validating those models — unconditional and conditional coverage backtesting under the Basel framework and the model-risk expectations of SR 11-7 — was designed for traditional parametric models. Using daily 2000–2026 data for six assets spanning equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, and cryptocurrency, we ask whether ML Value-at-Risk (VaR) models that satisfy standard backtests are reliable, or whether current validation confers false comfort. We evaluate four forecasters with a consolidated protocol that augments the Kupiec and Christoffersen tests with regime-conditional coverage, overfitting control, and conformal recalibration, mapped to the three pillars of model-risk governance. We document a pervasive and economically large result: models that pass the unconditional coverage test breach two to three times the target rate in stressed regimes at the 95% level, and five to nine times at the 99% level that underpins regulatory capital. Historical simulation passes the Kupiec test on all six assets at 95% while breaching at up to 3.3 times target in stress; a formal logistic test confirms that entering a stress regime multiplies breach odds roughly three- to fivefold (p < 0.001). The gradient-boosted model, competitive in calm markets, is the most fragile under stress. We package the protocol as a governance-grade scorecard for the safe deployment of AI in financial risk measurement.

detail.abstract: Workplace investigations sit at the intersection of employment law, organisational psychology, and human resource management. Yet many organisations lack consistent procedures for handling internal complaints, exposing employees to unfair treatment and employers to legal, reputational, and financial risks. This conceptual review synthesises peer-reviewed and professional literature on organisational justice, procedural fairness, employee voice and whistleblowing, sexual-harassment investigations, investigative interviewing, alternative dispute resolution, and the use of artificial intelligence in employee relations. Drawing on organisational justice and psychological-safety research, it identifies recurring weaknesses in investigation practice, including inadequate investigator training, inconsistent complaint intake, limited transparency, insufficient attention to trauma-informed interviewing, and weak governance of AI-assisted workflows. The paper proposes a conceptual framework that integrates procedural, interpersonal, informational, and distributive justice with legal-defensibility considerations across five stages: intake, planning, evidence gathering, determination, and resolution. It concludes by identifying priorities for future research, including longitudinal evaluation of investigation outcomes, cross-jurisdictional analysis of fairness standards, and empirical assessment of AI-assisted investigation tools. Because this is a conceptual review, the proposed framework requires empirical validation.

detail.abstract: In Western democratic capitalism, two figures hold the most influence over the economy: the President, who holds fiscal executive power, and the central bank chair, who holds monetary executive power. Their tolerance for risk therefore shapes policy and markets. We estimate the risk aversion of both U.S. executives from their choices within one strategic model. The Fed's risk aversion is its precautionary rate response to inflation uncertainty; the President's is the inverse of the policy risk he creates beyond what economic conditions warrant. Presidential risk aversion varies fourfold since 1985, with Trump's second term the most risk-tolerant, and Presidents turn cautious before midterm elections. The two risk aversions co-move, with the President leading the Fed by six to twelve months, and the Fed eases 0.75 percentage points per standard deviation of presidential policy risk. Markets track the Fed's precautionary stance: uncertainty and stock volatility rise with Fed risk aversion.

detail.abstract: We establish a near-optimal almost sure invariance principle for nonstationary time series under the functional dependence measure (FDM) framework. This result yields a universal time-uniform dependent central limit theorem, which serves as the basis for anytime-valid inference. In particular, we instantiate the theorem through asymptotic confidence sequences (AsympCSs), time-uniform counterparts of asymptotic confidence intervals obtained via central limit theorems, extending those originally proposed in Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) to time series with serial dependence. We further refine their definition because, as we show, it can admit AsympCSs that fail to achieve the desired asymptotic time-uniform coverage for a broad class of data-generating processes, including independent and identically distributed cases. We address this issue by adding a simple eventual-inclusion condition, which in turn permits more flexible variance estimation, particularly useful in time-series settings. For feasible implementation of AsympCSs, we establish strong consistency of HAC variance estimators under the FDM framework, accommodating a wider range of commonly used bandwidth choices than existing results under mixing conditions. As illustrations, we construct AsympCSs for algorithms with Markovian structure and time-series-based causal estimands.

detail.abstract: Climate change can reduce cold exposure while increasing heat exposure, making thermal-welfare change difficult to measure. The Thermal Deviation Index (TDI) applies a nonlinear, two-sided response function to temperature relative to a human-centered optimum and accumulates the resulting values over time. Higher TDI denotes greater accumulated deviation and lower thermal welfare. Across 243,616 land cells over 1940-2024, baseline thermal position predicts the direction of change, while migration and leisure choices are associated with lower-TDI environments. Increasing TDI is associated with lower national output and employment and greater heat-related work-hour losses. Among the population living in cells with increasing TDI, 52.1% experience displacement exceeding twice the local detrended variability. The share remains 40.1% after AR(1) adjustment. Under CMIP6 projections with fixed 2020 population weights, warming concentrates losses among warmer, lower-income populations. TDI provides an accounting measure for climate economics.

detail.abstract: Automated trading plays a major role in developed financial markets and is expanding in emerging markets. I study how homogeneity in automated trading decisions generates systemic risk and how regulation can contain it. I develop a continuous time model of a single trading day in which automated traders form correlated forecasts and operate at two speeds. Slow traders respond to the accumulated price movement, while fast traders respond to contemporaneous price changes. The price impact of their orders generates feedback, and leveraged positions face forced liquidation beyond a margin buffer. I measure systemic risk as the probability that the intraday dislocation exceeds a threshold defined relative to the same sector trading on uncorrelated signals. I analyze position limits, margin requirements, and a circuit breaker that reopens trading through a call auction. I show that greater market penetration, defined as sector size relative to residual market depth, lowers the critical homogeneity at which baseline stability is lost and increases the regulatory intensity required to contain risk. Under a strong auction pricing assumption, the reopening auction removes feedback amplification from the reopening price and reduces daily systemic risk. Illustrative calibrations for the United States, the European Union, and India show that rules calibrated to deep markets can leave thinner markets more exposed. These results support regulatory calibration that accounts for market depth, trading speed, and sector growth, particularly in rapidly automating emerging markets.

detail.abstract: Does vacant lot greening help resolve unpaid property taxes? We examine changes in property tax outcomes around Philadelphia's 2013-2018 greening installations using linked tax balances, assessments, and deeds. Arrears prevalence declines more in treated neighborhoods than in propensity-score-matched controls, by 0.9 percentage points averaged over the next three years; matching additionally on prior financial histories reduces the estimated difference to 0.4 percentage points. This attenuation points to the role of initial indebtedness. Treated neighborhoods begin with more indebted accounts, while exit probabilities among initial debtors are similar across groups. Among accounts owing comparable existing bills, we find little difference in bill persistence or sustained clearance, with about 22 percent in each group free of all arrears in all three annual follow-ups. Clearance more often involves sheriff deeds, which record court-ordered transfers, with the difference concentrated among accounts carrying older obligations. Our findings suggest that fiscal evaluations of neighborhood investment should track whether accounts remain free of arrears and whether existing owners retain their properties when unpaid taxes are resolved.

detail.abstract: A growing public record documents real-world harms involving artificial intelligence (AI) systems developed or deployed by public companies, but whether those incidents become identifiable in subsequent securities filings has not been systematically measured. We match 2019–2026 AI Incident Database (AIID) incidents (n = 1,389) to U.S.-listed domestic periodic-report filers, yielding 307 incidents involving 21 issuers. For each incident, we examine Forms 8-K, 10-K and 10-Q filed during the following 12 months and code the strongest disclosure as incident-specific (T1), disclosure of a directly related legal consequence without identifying the incident (T2), generic risk language addressing the same technology or harm family (T3), or no related disclosure located (T4). Under the pre-registered coding, there are 4 T1, 3 T2, 278 T3 and 22 T4 incidents. Incident-specific disclosure therefore occurs in 1.3% of incidents (Clopper–Pearson 95% CI, 0.4–3.3), while T1+T2 substantive disclosure occurs in 2.3% (0.9–4.6) as an upper bound. The remaining 300 incidents (97.7%, 95.4–99.1) form the AI incident disclosure shadow: no incident-specific or directly related legal-consequence disclosure was identifiable in the specified filing universe. Among T3 incidents, only 84 match both the incident's AI application family and harm family, while 194 match only one. In all, 70.4% of all incidents (64.9–75.4) therefore have at most weakly related filing language. In exploratory analyses, no severity gradient is detectable and the apparent association with issuer role is fragile to specification and single-case changes. The seven substantive cases cluster around financial-statement effects or formal legal and regulatory consequences, including reported financial impacts of approximately $304 million and $478 million. These estimates are conditional on AIID recording and issuer resolvability and measure visibility in Forms 8-K, 10-K and 10-Q, not legal compliance or all investor-facing communication.

detail.abstract: This study examines draw-or-stand decisions that maximize expected net profit in a specified model of Pok Deng (ป๊อกเดง้) with one player and one dealer, a standard 52-card deck reshuffled for every round, and a fixed one-unit stake. The hand hierarchy, from highest to lowest, is Pok 9, Pok 8, three of a kind, straight flush, straight or three face cards, and ordinary point hands. Special hands in the same tier tie without further point comparison. A three-card flush that is neither a straight nor another special hand remains an ordinary point hand, but pays three units when it wins. The dealer follows a fixed policy: draw below five points and stand on five through seven points. We first prove that the player’s expected value (EV) is zero when both sides use this same policy, given symmetric dealing, policies, and payouts. We then use 1,000,000,000 Monte Carlo training rounds to estimate the returns from drawing and standing with shared latent cards, select an action for each of 169 initial-hand classes, and freeze the resulting policy before evaluating it on 100,000,000 new rounds. The learned policy achieves a held-out EV of +0.009367890 units per unit staked, or +0.936789%. Its paired improvement over the baseline is +0.954484 percentage points, with a 95% confidence interval of [+0.948788, +0.960180] percentage points. Exact enumeration gives an EV of +0.955872584% and confirms that the learned policy selects the optimal action for all 137 decision-eligible hand classes; the remaining 32 classes are forced initial Pok hands. Only nine classes change from standing to drawing, together affecting 5.621449% of all rounds after accounting for the requirement that the dealer has no initial Pok. These findings establish a best response to the specified fixed dealer under the stated rules and information constraints. They do not guarantee profit over every finite period or establish optimality against every dealer policy.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how accumulating production emissions affect the valuation of future environmental impacts compared to consumption. In order to examine the subject in detail, this study uses a Ramsey-Koopmans framework that merges consumption utility with environmental impact that increases quadratically with pollution stock. In addition, it also uses virgin cotton and polyester fiber emissions attributed to the clothing industry, assuming constant annual emissions and an approximate persistence function. The environmental rate in the paper is calculated as pure time preference minus the proportional growth rate of marginal damage. This established rate stays lower than the consumption-based discount rate at the evaluated dates because accumulated pollution stock directly leads to increases in marginal damage. As the proportional stock growth slows, the environmental rate rises, even as stock and damage levels continue to increase. Separately, this model highlights that lower emissions reduce modeled harm without changing the rate, given that persistence weights remain fixed and initial stock is zero. The findings allow for differentiating the amount of environmental damage from the changes in its discounted marginal welfare weight. Additionally, it confirms that accumulation must be taken into consideration when assessing the production of "green" materials and techniques, while remaining conditional on the model's assumptions.

detail.abstract: The Formula 1 cost cap, in force since 2021, was introduced partly to support competitive balance. This paper asks whether the performance gap between teams narrowed after the cap, and whether teams with broader precap resources lost ground relative to others. Using race and qualifying data for 2005 to 2025 and approximated pre-cap budgets for ten team lineages, it takes each team's qualifying gap to pole as the primary outcome. Among the nine teams that raced in every season since 2014, the average gap fell by approximately 0.5 to 0.6 percentage points of lap time from 2021, depending on whether each team's fastest car or the average of both cars is used, with no significant additional change in 2022 and no clear linear trend. Points-based concentration measures and the persistence of the constructors' order did not change detectably. At the team level, higher precap budgets are associated with a relative increase in qualifying gap after 2021 (coefficient 0.25; permutation p = 0.16), but the estimate is imprecise and depends largely on Mercedes. The cap cannot be separated from other regulatory changes in 2021 and 2022, and only five cap-era seasons are available. The evidence is consistent with narrower pace differences after 2021 but does not show that the cap caused them.

detail.abstract:
Article 14 of the EU AI Act requires high-risk AI systems to be designed so that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. This paper asks what documentary evidence organisations should preserve, and inspectors should examine, to establish whether a specified runtime human-review obligation was carried out in high-stakes, regulated settings.

We propose a structured record with four elements: form, support, correspondence and coverage. It records prescribed and evidenced practice separately; asks whether the relevant actor was provisioned for the task; tests whether evidenced performance carried out the same underlying control function as the prescription; and records how much of the governed work that performance reached. An unexplained absence of evidence remains indeterminable rather than being treated as non-performance.

We also distinguish separable review from human control fused with performance of the underlying task. Where review must be evidenced as a distinct activity, the workflow must provide both a separable review activity or control point and a recording arrangement that makes its performance or omission identifiable.

The paper proposes a documentary representation rather than a validated measure of oversight effectiveness. We recommend that the Commission pilot it as a candidate structure for practical guidance under Article 96, and adopt it only if testing shows that the required information can be recovered from realistic organisational records, applied consistently by different analysts and retained at proportionate cost.

detail.abstract: We study how retained ownership supports the value of a zero-dividend asset held for resale. A sponsor chooses hidden maintenance that determines market survival, bears full cost, and captures benefits only through retained tokens. A positive stationary equilibrium exists if and only if retention exceeds an endogenous minimum, and extra curvature restrictions yield two equilibria. Conditional on survival, prices below the upper equilibrium converge to the lower one. Credible news that future retention falls below the minimum causes immediate collapse through backward unraveling. Thus, insider unlocks affect valuation via governance without changing token supply or cash flows.

detail.abstract: This article analyzes the role of frozen Russian sovereign assets in bridging the gap between Russia’s legal obligation to make reparation and the delivery of compensation to Ukraine. In doing so, it examines Ukraine’s emerging reparations architecture and assesses proposals for use of the frozen assets in future compensation efforts. The article argues that any Russian sovereign assets lawfully made available for reparative purposes should be directed through a dedicated compensation fund linked to the International Claims Commission and used to satisfy awards arising from Russia’s internationally wrongful acts. While this institutional approach does not resolve the contested legal basis for transferring the assets, it offers a framework for translating Russia’s legal responsibility into meaningful redress for Ukraine.

detail.abstract: The article summarises a research programme in which society is treated as an adaptive system. Its capacity to respond to changes in the environment depends on how it defines a legitimate leader, how it selects people for positions of power and influence, and whether it can revise the rules of selection themselves. The programme is reduced to two original elements. The first is the Picaro and Janteloven corridor: a zone of norms in which initiat ive is not suppressed by levelling pressure, exploitation and deception are restrained, and ideals are constantly checked against reality. The second is a school programme in recognising manipulative behaviour, narcissistic traits and Machiavellianism, intended to make the selection of leaders more resistant to manipulation. Together they describe a secular restoration of the ethical content of religious ideals of service without a religious foundation. The article also develops a hypothesis about modernity: the next leap in Western economic growth depends on opening social lifts. All claims are presented as testable hypotheses with indicators and falsification conditions, and the results of the quantitative tests already carried out are reported without smoothing.

detail.abstract: In May 2026, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) proposed giving public companies the option to replace their three quarterly reports on Form 10-Q with a single semiannual report on Form 10-S. The proposal drew more than 215,000 public comments, an extraordinary number for a disclosure rule. Using a large language model (LLM) guided by a theory-based codebook, we classify every comment by who wrote it, what position it took, how it justified that position, and how it described the proposal. We then examine how positions, arguments, and tone differ across commenter types and over the comment period. Three findings stand out. First, in sharp contrast to comment letters on accounting standards, which come predominantly from organizations, individuals wrote nearly all of the comments; many identify as retail investors or retirees, and organizations account for less than 0.1%. Most comments are measured or emphatic in tone. The 5.6% that use hostile language come mainly from commenters who do not identify themselves, and such language is nearly absent from organizational letters. Second, opposition is nearly unanimous (97.8%). Opponents defend quarterly reporting on principle, citing transparency, accountability, and timely information, rather than on economic consequences. Most commenters give reasons, but few offer input a regulator could use to redesign the rule, and most of the alternatives they propose call for more frequent reporting. Only among trade associations does a substantial share support the proposal, citing reporting costs and the case for letting companies choose their reporting frequency. Third, the comments allow us to test a view the SEC expressed after the comment period closed: that opposition reflected a misunderstanding of the proposal. Only 2.6% of comments describe the proposal as abolishing quarterly reporting, and commenters who describe it as optional oppose it just as firmly. A subsequent wave of more than 40,000 letters, many from people who had already commented, insisted that their writers understood the proposal but was shorter, less often reasoned, and more often hostile. We discuss implications for due process and stakeholder participation in disclosure regulation.

detail.abstract: China's 1999 university expansion nearly doubled college enrollment overnight. Combining countylevel difference-indifferences with a Bartik-style pull factor across five census waves (1990-2015), we show that the expansion raised minority women's in-migration to university-dense counties by 2 percentage points, roughly double the effect for minority men and at least as large as either Han group's response. This response is broadly distributed rather than concentrated among minority women in a particular subgroup or place. The expansion's effects extend beyond migrants themselves: non-migrant girls in high-exposure provinces remain in school longer, and complementary evidence shows higher employment among expansion-eligible minority women. These results suggest that a gender-neutral supply-side policy can broadly reshape minority women's educational and geographic opportunities.
