detail.abstract: Hedonic house-price models are bounded by the characteristics an analyst can measure, yet much of a home's value is recorded only in the free-text description and photographs of its listing. We treat general-purpose AI models as a feature-engineering technology for hedonic analysis: a large language model converts each description into structured property specifications, and a vision–language model converts the façade photograph into visual attributes, both under strict JSON schemas that make the outputs auditable econometric variables. Using 19,123 Quebec house listings, the two AI layers raise the R^2 of an already rich log-linear hedonic specification with municipality fixed effects from 0.717 to 0.755, 3.0 of the 3.8 points coming from the façade photograph, and they raise the out-of-sample R^2 of every estimator from OLS to gradient boosting and neural networks (best ensemble: R^2 of 0.779, median absolute error 14.0%). The vision layer adds more to the linear model than switching from OLS to a random forest does. The extracted attributes carry economically sensible implicit prices—2.3% per point of curb appeal, 3–4% for brick or stone façades—that survive municipality-clustered inference, a cluster bootstrap, postal-code fixed effects, and a control for the language of the description, which itself carries a 7% conditional premium for English listings. We also document that for-sale-by-owner descriptions embed the asking price, so that the text layer's gain is credible only on the brokered platform, and that spatially grouped cross-validation lowers all accuracy levels by three to five points while preserving the AI increments.

detail.abstract: Regulations aimed at correcting under-investment in a technology, often omit margins of allocation that determine how much of its social benefits are realized. I study this problem using California’s battery storage mandate which induced battery investment, with an explicit goal to reduce congestion and the resulting need for transmission upgrade, without compensating the location-specific congestion relief provided by this investment. Using a constructed dataset that combines hourly prices at 2,203 pricing nodes over 2011-2022 and the staggered launch of 80 battery sites, I find that battery entry compresses local congestion prices towards zero, in line with the purpose of the regulation. However, these benefits vary widely across locations. Specifically, they fall with the depth of pre-existing local congestion. As an extreme example, six of California’s fifteen largest battery sites currently provide no estimated congestion relief at their realized locations. A counterfactual exercise indicates that reallocating the same fifteen batteries while holding battery sizes, commissioning years, and utility territories fixed roughly doubles their estimated congestion relief. This would save an additional $126 − 151 million in congestion charges over their ten year life cycles, saving which would otherwise require $20-$80 million dollars in transmission upgrade investment in the long run.

title: Transformer-Based Dynamic Compressed Sensing for Indoor Millimeter-Wave Target Tracking Under a Limited Observation Budget

detail.title: Transformer-Based Dynamic Compressed Sensing for Indoor Millimeter-Wave Target Tracking Under a Limited Observation Budget
detail.abstract: To address the observation requirements of high-dimensional radio-frequency features in indoor millimeter-wave target tracking, this paper proposes a Transformer-based dynamic compressed-sensing tracking method that integrates history-driven observation selection, mask-aware sparse encoding, auxiliary reconstruction with a dynamic dictionary, and causal temporal estimation. Historical context and the positional uncertainty from the preceding frame determine the current observation budget and element selection. A binary observation mask is constructed, and the partial observations and mask are jointly encoded into a shared sparse representation. A low-rank dynamic dictionary is conditioned on the historical state, while auxiliary reconstruction and observed-element consistency constraints support representation learning. The shared sparse representation and historical context are supplied to a causal Transformer to estimate the current position and its uncertainty. The updated state is fed back to subsequent observation selection and dictionary adaptation, forming a continuous tracking loop. Simulation and measured-data experiments show that the proposed method achieves continuous indoor target tracking from limited RF feature observations and provides positional uncertainty estimates.

detail.abstract: Negative-risk events on Polymarket list one binary contract for every outcome of a decision and settle exactly one of them at one dollar, so that their prices are observable analogues of Arrow–Debreu state prices. We use the five-outcome market on the June 2026 FOMC decision (146 daily closes, December 2025 to May 2026) and the seventeen-contract market on the 2024 U.S. presidential election (304 daily closes) to ask how the Arrow–Debreu pricing restrictions fare in a blockchain market. Because spanning is built into the contract design, the testable content is the law of one price for the complete set of claims, whose executable no-arbitrage bounds we derive from the platform's minting and conversion mechanics. The sum of state prices averages 1.017 (Fed) and 1.015 (election); the overround is statistically positive but of the order of the quoted half-spreads of the low-priced legs, declines steadily towards resolution, reverts within two days, and is bracketed by the bid- and ask-side sums of the order book. It has the wrong sign to be explained by the time value of money, which places the complete set below one. The normalised prices define a risk-neutral distribution over the FOMC decision whose mean—a Polymarket analogue of the futures-implied expected policy change—moves two to five times more, in variance terms, on FOMC and employment-report days than on other days, while weekend trading carries about one third of weekday variance. Once Polymarket closes are aligned to the U.S. trading calendar and lag orders are chosen by information criteria, daily changes in this measure neither lead nor lag the ten-year Treasury yield, the S&P 500, the VIX or Bitcoin. We document how a one-day misalignment of blockchain time stamps and a minimum-p lag search generated spurious lead–lag findings in an earlier version.

detail.abstract: This paper asks under what conditions inherited wealth, mortgage leverage, nominal debt, housing supply and down-payment constraints generate persistent owner–renter wealth gaps among households with the same labour-income process, and what an unanticipated inflation changes. A three-stage benchmark with two-period generations yields a closed-form ownership-entry threshold that adds a liquidity component to the down-payment bound, a leverage multiplier whose break-even price growth is independent of the loan-to-value ratio, a closed-form intergenerational tenure persistence that is positive only if the house is net wealth at the end of life, existence and a uniqueness condition for the stationary equilibrium, and the accounting of a price-level surprise under three mortgage contracts. A twelve-period overlapping-generations model with nominal annuity mortgages, gifts and estates, and segmented rental and construction sectors is solved in stationary general equilibrium and along perfect-foresight transitions under an illustrative calibration. Transfers generate a income-year wealth gap at mid-life and a rank–rank wealth slope of that vanishes without transfers; price adjustment removes –% of the partial-equilibrium ownership response to the down-payment constraint; no multiple equilibria arise under near-fixed supply. Because households are net nominal creditors, a 10% surprise moves the real house price by %, a fall where the benchmark predicts a rise; the contract ordering, fixed-rate above renewable term above adjustable, is confirmed.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how search frictions, heterogeneous seller urgency, financing frictions and bargaining jointly determine the liquidity discount, transaction prices, sale hazards and price dispersion in a local housing market. In a continuous-time matching model with free entry of buyers, sellers differ in a permanent carrying cost, buyers draw match-specific valuations, and prices are set by Nash bargaining. The urgency discount, defined relative to the most patient seller, is nonnegative and increasing in the carrying cost, and the expected price falls by less than the reservation price. A fall in buyer arrivals or in mortgage qualification lowers prices, lengthens time on market and widens the discount when the valuation distribution has an increasing failure rate; with heavy-tailed valuations a more liquid market can lengthen time on market, under an explicit condition on the carrying cost. Liquidity shocks move prices, volume, inventory and durations with no change in housing-service values, and buyer entry amplifies them. The gap between mortgage and cash prices decomposes into a delay-bargaining term that rises with urgency, an outside-option term, and a selection term that can be negative. The composition of transactions shifts after a liquidity shock in a direction governed by the shape of the valuation distribution, and its effect on a transaction-price index is an order of magnitude smaller than the within-type liquidity effect, which no quality adjustment removes. The Walrasian free-entry price is shown not to be a liquidity premium benchmark, since search prices exceed it in thick markets. Results are illustrated numerically with a documented parameterisation and reproducible code; no data are used.

detail.abstract: Clinicians who use AI-based decision support rely on it badly in both directions: they follow wrong advice (misuse) and they reject right advice (disuse). Separately, a growing set of benchmarks shows that large language models answer clinical questions with recommendations that have since been superseded, and that the date up to which a model knows the literature is neither sharp nor the one declared. Engineering work on time-aware and version-aware retrieval makes answers more current; it does not tell the clinician which answers are. We argue that the two findings meet in a single requirement: reliance can only be calibrated against an answer that states on which version of the evidence it rests and whether that version is still in force at the moment of use. We call such an answer a dated answer, state its requirements, and read them through four states of warrant (provisional, validated, valid, valued) that apply to any knowledge with a horizon of validity. We then propose an evaluation design, to be specified in detail for pre-registration, that measures clinicians' reliance against the declared limit, with current and superseded advice, and so separates the misuse of stale advice from the disuse of current advice. The legal domain, where a public source states which provisions were in force at any date, serves as the reference case. We close with a research agenda.

detail.abstract: Night-time lights are widely used as a proxy for local economic welfare, yet most evidence predates the COVID-19 shock and relies on cross-sectional validation. I assemble a complete departmentyear panel for Peru (25 departments, 20152024) combining ocial monetary poverty rates, a full replication of the ocial estimates from ENAHO microdata (mean absolute replication error of 0.20 percentage points across 170 published cells), VIIRS V.2 annual night-light composites, and structural household covariates. Within a FayHerriot small-area framework estimated by REML with parametric-bootstrap MSE, night lights alone reduce between-department variance by under 10% and do not improve leave-one-out predictive accuracy over an intercept-only model (11.73 vs. 11.71 pp). Three structural covariateselectricity access, dirt-oor share, and sewerageexplain 58%; adding lights raises this to 67%. The unconditional lightspoverty correlation collapses after 2020, from-0.41 (2015) to-0.10 (2024), as the pandemic shifted Peru's poverty map toward dense, brightly lit urban areas; conditional on services, brighter departments are poorer. Results are robust to the VIIRS V.2/V2.2 version break (excluding 20222024 leaves coecients unchanged). The ndings caution against luminosity-only poverty mapping in middle-income, urbanizing settings and quantify how much conventional structural covariates still matter.

detail.abstract: Between 2012 and 2025 the United States and the Central Bank of Iraq barred 33 Iraqi banks from the dollar: 46 percent of all licenses, half the private banks, about a tenth of banking assets; the 22 banks the Union of Arab Banks counted as barred in spring 2024 had carried about a third of the dollars the window sold. This paper builds the first dated series of those restrictions and asks what they did to bank intermediation. The answer, in the aggregates: less than either side claims. The bundled shock of November 2022, the electronic screening platform together with bans on the four banks that carried 40 percent of window flow, raised excess reserves about 20 percent and cut the money multiplier 4.6 percent on impact; the later bans show only transitory hoarding, gone within eighteen months, with the Central Bank's own policy rate explaining the parking thereafter. The aggregates bound, rather than measure, losses inside the restricted banks, which hold about 2 percent of deposits. The multiplier never exceeded 1.47 because the banks were never lenders: in 2012 to 2017 the window rent pool ran 1.06 to 1.76 times the system's entire potential net interest income, and the window banks' own accounts show 68 to 83 percent of operating income from commissions and currency, not loans. A counterfactual in the author's structural model prices the ban-era hoard at 0.3 to 2.8 percent of one year's GDP, against about 7.5 percent of GDP forgone in every year that the counter, rather than a lending system, allocates the deposits.

detail.abstract:
This paper develops a microfounded, stock-flow consistent (SFC) non-linear macroeconomic framework with heterogeneous firms to study how short-term liquidity shocks and public procurement payment arrears (tt) drive dynamic asset misallocation and permanent losses in measured Total Factor Productivity (TFP). Grounded in the modern literature on micro-to-macro misallocation, we formalize industrial dynamics as a non-linear system where physical production frontiers are exogenously given, but measured aggregate efficiency is endogenously distorted by financial balance-sheet constraints. Heterogeneous firms navigate an environment characterized by asymmetric credit markets, where a binding Operating Liquidity Constraint (ait = a) conditions capability accumulation. Boundedly rational managers select between an Innovative Routine (I), which commits resources to cross the technological frontier but compresses liquidity cushions, and a defensive, non-innovative Trinchera Routine (T). We model an asymmetric credit friction where smaller, highly productive firms are locked out of factoring markets due to prohibitive endogenous sovereign-risk discount rates, forcing them to absorb the state delay. Conversely, large technically stagnant incumbents leverage collateral cushions to act as transaction rent-extracting financial intermediaries over the supply chain.
We aggregate these microeconomic transactional rules into a low-dimensional non-linear dynamical system governing the market share of innovative firms (xt). Utilizing a smooth logistic approximation to secure C2 regularity, we analytically derive the critical public payment threshold (tc). We prove that when state arrears exceed this endogenous boundary, the macroeconomic system undergoes a local transcritical bifurcation where a native eigenvalue of the Jacobian matrix crosses zero, fulfilling strict transversality conditions. This phase transition triggers a process of Spurious Destruction: the market selection filter detaches from physical capability and aligns with balance-sheet resilience, forcing a dynamic misallocation that drives the aggregate resource covariance into strictly negative boundaries. We formalize how the reallocation of market shares toward large, scale-inefficient incumbents induces a permanent productivity scar through the destruction of firm-specific capital and dynamic skills-attrition under endogenous tech-entry barriers. Finally, we establish the macroeconomic limits of a counter-cyclical tax-displacement synchronization scheme managed by the federal tax authority (AFIP). We prove that under a systemic fiscal crisis, the automated tax deferral risks eroding the tax base completely, triggering a fiscal-dominance feedback loop that forces monetary-backed spending, returning the inflationary tax to the system and destabilizing the phase-space topology. A mathematical appendix formally derives the transversality conditions and the macro-fiscal budget boundary

detail.abstract: We study a multi-player communication-coordnation game in which privately informed agents communicate through a social network and choose their optimal actions while balancing it against their own bliss points and that of the neighbours actions. We show that equilibrium actions are convex combinations of the expected bliss points of all players, with weights being determined by a degree-discounted Bonacich centrality measure. We also characterize when players report truthfully, over-report, or under-report their private information, and show that the incentive to misreport depends critically on the receiver's position in the network. A striking implication is that even under identical preferences fully revealing communication may not realise and information transmission may remain coarse in a star network while becoming almost fully informative in a complete network. Finally, when biases are endogenously chosen, strategic responses to neighbours' biases are governed by their centralities, and unbiasedness may emerge as a Nash equilibrium.

detail.abstract: The latest reading of inflation in central sectors with rigid prices (RC) can be reconstructed from public data (3.29% for August 2026 against the published 3.3%), and its gap to actual headline inflation is almost fully explained by item coverage and the aggregation method. However, the Bank of England's empirical claim that RC better reflects the output gap is not confirmed with public gap measures, and RC adds no confirmed predictive power in out-of-sample forecasts of future headline inflation. For a main composite measure of labour-market pressure, RC's in-sample same-quarter R² point estimate is higher than those of the baseline comparison indices (services, core, headline and CPI84) and of composition control indices, and nominal additional information remains in regressions that control for services. The stand-alone fit is, however, highly sensitive to whether 2022-23 is included, and in the current direct four-quarter-ahead forecasting specification adding RC to services yields no realised forecasting gain. For energy pass-through, point estimates of the pipeline increase are positive in all 18 lag specifications examined, but their size is sensitive to specification and sample, and the interval for the baseline specification includes zero. The quantitative paths are conditional on the model and on the assumed energy price path. The paper and replication code are also available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23550468.

affiliations: Universidad Diego Portales

detail.title: Tax Revenue in the Euro Area: Oil-Price News and Fiscal Space
detail.abstract: Can inflationary oil-price shocks increase tax receipts enough to create fiscal space? I estimate euro-area and member-state revenue responses over 2004–2024 using high-frequency oil-price surprises around OPEC announcements and the corresponding proxy-VAR-implied shock. Total euro-area revenue relative to GDP shows no statistically significant increase over the following three years. For a 10-log-point increase in the real oil price, first-year 90 percent Anderson– Rubin confidence sets place upper bounds of 0.121 and 0.041 percentage points of GDP on the revenue response under the two measures. The full member-state panel exhibits a short- lived rise in VAT/GDP but no comparable gain in other product taxes; the VAT estimate is sensitive to excluding the pandemic period. A small-open-economy model explains how external consumption smoothing can raise VAT relative to GDP even as imported energy reduces national income. At unchanged tax rates, the model establishes a non-positive discounted VAT/GDP response and a fall in the present value of total tax receipts. Evidence on relative prices and external adjustment is consistent with key elements of the mechanism, although not all cross- country predictions hold. The distinction between tax-base inflation and intertemporal fiscal resources matters for the financing of energy-price relief.

detail.abstract:
Every counter-architecture in the Indic Futures series (Bandvi, 2026a–2026i) presupposes a mind that has had the chance to form: an adult who can practise Viveka, notice the pull of a feed, and return attention to a chosen object. This paper asks what happens when the mind being engineered is still being built. It argues that the Indic tradition’s first ashrama, Brahmacharya, understood childhood as a protected period of formation, and that this understanding yields a positive specification of what children’s environments must provide. The specification holds however the contested causal evidence on screens and adolescent mental health is eventually resolved.

India is a demanding setting for the argument. The ASER 2024 rural survey found smartphones present in about 90% of surveyed households, yet most 14–16-year-olds do not own one: the typical Indian digital child shares a family device, and the gender gap in ownership (36.2% of boys, 26.9% of girls) means that protection and exclusion can be confused. India’s policy window is open: the Economic Survey 2025–26 named digital addiction a public-health concern, the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 put verifiable parental consent and limits on tracking and targeted advertising for under-18s into force in May 2027, and state governments announced age limits in March 2026.

The paper introduces five constructs. Developmental Sovereignty is a child’s claim to complete the formation of foundational capacities before becoming a primary target of optimisation. Premature Closure is the algorithmic foreclosure of identity before exploration, which in India compounds with early academic tracking. Guru Substitution Risk names the filling of the teacher’s role by entities that lack the teacher’s accountability, assessed by a four-part Guru Accountability Test (knowledge, answerability, refusal, redundancy). The Brahmacharya Environment Standard (BES) specifies five conditions for homes, schools and child-facing products: Undistracted Hours, Productive Difficulty, Accountable Presence, Daily Rhythm, and Real Service. The Formation Exposure Index (FEI) measures the engineered and formative quality of a child’s waking hours, and is deliberately not a screen-time counter.

The paper treats Brahmacharya’s historical exclusions by caste and gender as a defect to be rejected, extracts the developmental principle, and ends with graduated release (samavartana): protection is justified only as preparation for freedom. It evaluates age-limit policy by three tests (formation, equity, release), states two falsifiable propositions, and outlines a pre-registered school pilot. The constructs are conceptual and unvalidated; the paper is a base for research, not a verdict.

title: When Cold Reverses Load Shifting: Weather and the Limits of Time-of-Use Pricing for Electric Vehicle Charging

detail.abstract: Time-of-use pricing is the main tool for moving electric vehicle charging out of congested hours, and its load-shifting effect is usually treated as a fixed parameter of demand. Using 250,669 public charging sessions at 13 stations in Jiaxing, China, matched to daily weather, we show that the response is not fixed and that its sign depends on the weather. Under heavy rain and extreme heat, charging moves toward off-peak hours, as the tariff intends. Under extreme cold it moves the other way: peak-period participation falls by 5.5 percentage points and sharp-peak participation rises by 5.6 percentage points, a near one-for-one swap into the most expensive hours, with no offsetting rise in off-peak charging. An exact session-level log decomposition, ln(power) = ln(energy) - ln(duration), identifies the mechanism. Cold acts through delivered power, which declines monotonically with temperature and is 9.9% lower on days averaging below freezing. The constraint is common across charger types, and drivers absorb it only partly: connection time lengthens 3.5% while session energy still falls. Because dwell time is set by the driver's schedule, session energy rises with temperature across the cold range. This is the opposite of the U-shape that engineering models predict for consumption per kilometer, so load models calibrated on public charging data will get the sign wrong in winter. At the station level, an extreme cold day lowers total load by 3.1% and raises sharp-peak load by 20.6%. Charging flexibility is a state, not a property.

detail.abstract: This paper compares the adoption, diffusion and penetration of the internet and of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in six regions: Africa, South Africa, Asia-Pacific (including Oceania), Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC), North America and Europe. Every quantity is expressed relative to the United States. Building on Amavilah (2009) and Asongu et al. (2020), diffusion enters a relative technology equation, which feeds a relative production function with transitional capital dynamics and then a human-development equation. Regional AI levels and diffusion speeds are computed from Microsoft country data (Microsoft AI Economy Institute, 2026a), weighted by population. Nested logistic diffusion curves then project relative internet and AI use to 2031 and 2036. Relative internet gaps close everywhere. Africa's absolute AI-use gap to the US roughly doubles, from 21 to 41 percentage points, and Asia-Pacific's and LAC's gaps widen until about 2031 before narrowing. Europe currently leads the US in AI use, but its lead erodes as both approach saturation. Over a decade the digital channel raises relative GDP per capita by about 4% in Africa, 2% in Asia-Pacific and LAC, 1.4% in South Africa and 0.3% in North America, and lowers it by 0.5% in Europe. Effects on TFP and HDI are smaller still. A 5,000-draw Monte Carlo over structural, diffusion and baseline parameters puts Africa's ten-year digital gain at 2.0-8.1% (90% interval) under the log-relative specification, with a gain in over 99% of draws. Under the level specification, the probability of any gain falls to 0.72. An out-of-sample back-test, fitting the diffusion curves on 2005-2017 and extrapolating to 2023, overstates Africa's internet use by 16 percentage points, so Africa's projected path should be read as optimistic. Two propositions characterise exactly when AI can narrow the ratio gap to the US while widening the absolute gap, and show that this is when the two specifications disagree in sign.

detail.abstract: The increasing scale of the national economy conceals a declining household income fraction fueling the U.S. standard of living. Measured using the Consumer Expenditure Survey, 1980-2025, 1.03 million observations, in 2025:Q1 one in three Americans (114.6 million) had outlays greater than after-tax income, including 74 percent in the lowest three deciles. Also, budgetary burdens have intensified since 2021. These realities motivate the Social Reserve, a $300 monthly tax free distribution to adult U.S. citizens totaling $1,776 billion by January 2029, financed with a special class of Federal Reserve liabilities. Methods from cosmic microwave background literature classify per-capita balances into four liquidity conditions. The 'gyre,' comprised of ordinary positive and negative balances, held 140.0 million people in 2025:Q1, 40.1 deficit and 99.9 surplus. In deficit below the gyre, 74.5 million, 122.0 million in surplus above. Spending was fitted locally across incomes from 2001:Q2. In simulation draws, 2025:Q1 households were exposed for 24 successive months, with residuals retiring debt or adding surpluses.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how the presence of captive consumers, who buy exclusively through a manufacturer's authorized sales channel, affects the profitability of unauthorized resale. I consider a model in which a manufacturer sells a good in two markets at different prices. This price difference creates an arbitrage opportunity for a reseller, who can buy the good in the low-price market and resell it in the high-price market. I show that the reseller's profit may increase with the share of captive consumers, although its potential customer base declines. This is because a higher degree of consumer captivity enables the manufacturer to sustain larger price differences between the markets, thereby increasing the reseller's margin. Hence, an implication of the paper is that measures aimed at increasing consumer captivity can have the unintended effect of making unauthorized resale more profitable.

detail.abstract: The United Kingdom lacks a consistent neighbourhood-level measure of accessibility by different transport modes, limiting understanding on spatial inequalities in the provision of public infrastructure. To address this, I use improvements in the availability of accurate driving and General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) information to provide population accessibility measures for 46,844 neighbourhoods across the UK. This uses mode-specific origin-destination pairs, providing data for over 1.5 billion journeys. The publicly available dataset and visualisation tool include: (i) a UK comparative relative accessibility index calculated through exponentially weighted time distances between population weighted neighbourhood centroids, (ii) a modal adequacy measure for each neighbourhood, showing how closely each mode (car, public transport, or combined car-public transport) encapsulates destination-specific fastest-mode accessibility; and, (iii) population reachable within intervals between 30 and 180 minutes across these modes. These data are directly compatible with other UK official statistics on, for instance, built environment and deprivation levels, providing a more solid foundation for more tailored place-based policies, a better examination of determinants of productivity and growth, and appreciation of the inequalities lost by aggregation.

detail.abstract: Firms increasingly collect diverse streams of customer data, including purchases, location visits, browsing activity, and other behavioral signals. While these data create new opportunities for customer understanding and personalization, they are often sparse, heterogeneous, and distributed across multiple sources, making it difficult to extract customer insights that generalize across marketing applications. We propose a framework for learning semantic customer embeddings that combines the semantic knowledge encoded in large language models (LLMs) with behavioral patterns observed in proprietary customer data. The framework uses LLM embeddings to initialize the representations of items observed within customer touchpoints, such as products purchased and retailers visited, adapts these representations to reflect observed behavioral context, and aggregates them across touchpoints into unified customer embeddings trained to capture future behavior. Using data from a large customer engagement platform, we show that the resulting embeddings provide meaningful representations of customers that can be used across multiple marketing applications, including customer segmentation and persona development, natural language look-alike audience discovery, and targeting newly introduced products. Together, our results demonstrate how semantically informed and behaviorally grounded customer embeddings provide a scalable foundation for customer analytics and personalization across diverse marketing decisions.

detail.abstract: Electoral systems differ in whether votes are pooled nationwide or aggregated within territorial units, such as regions. A common view holds that counting regions rather than voters pushes parties toward targeted regional spending at the expense of broad public goods. We revisit this view when parties compete with two complementary instruments: a national policy, which uses no budget, and transfers to regions. In our model, two office-seeking parties choose both, and voters in two ideologically distinct regions respond to each. When both regions are needed to win, territorial aggregation lets parties combine ideology and money to appeal to different regions, so they can offer divergent national policies. With nationwide vote counting, by contrast, parties either converge on the same policy and compete only through transfers or, if regions differ in size, no pure-strategy equilibrium exists. Counting regions can thus broaden, rather than narrow, the choices offered to voters.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest

detail.abstract: Digital marketing has become the main channel through which tourists discover, evaluate and choose destinations, yet evidence from emerging island destinations outside Bali remains fragmented. This working paper examines how digital marketing operates within the tourism ecosystem of West Nusa Tenggara (Nusa Tenggara Barat, NTB), with Lombok as the focal case. Using a qualitative integrative case study design, we analyse a purposive corpus of empirical and applied studies conducted in NTB, with particular attention to research produced by scholars at Sekolah Tinggi Pariwisata (STP) Mataram, the province's specialised tourism higher education institution. Thematic analysis of the corpus yields five themes: (1) a platform-led but website-weak digital presence among travel businesses and tourism villages; (2) the central role of electronic word-of-mouth and peer influence in converting attention into visit decisions; (3) persistent gaps in community-level digital capability among tourism awareness groups (Pokdarwis), village managers and micro-enterprises; (4) an emerging frontier of data analytics, automation and financial analytics in tourism marketing; and (5) the embedding of digital marketing in sustainability and multi-stakeholder governance agendas. Building on these themes and on resourcebased and dynamic capability perspectives, we propose a Digital Destination Marketing Capability (DDMC) framework comprising four capability domains (digital presence, community digital capability, data and intelligence, and governance and sustainability), linked to visitor and destination outcomes through eWOM, information credibility, destination image and co-created narratives. We derive five research propositions and outline practical implications for provincial tourism authorities, destination managers, travel businesses and tourism educators in NTB.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital banking has transformed the delivery of financial services in Nigeria, creating opportunities for convenience, accessibility and operational efficiency while intensifying concerns about transaction failures, cybersecurity, privacy and customer confidence. This article develops a conceptual framework for examining the relationship between digital banking service quality and customer loyalty, with customer satisfaction specified as a mediating variable and customer trust as a moderating variable. Drawing on the expectation-confirmation perspective, the technology acceptance literature, electronic service quality theory and relationship marketing theory, the article conceptualises digital banking service quality through reliability, efficiency, system availability, security and privacy, responsiveness, and ease of use. It proposes that higher perceived service quality increases customer satisfaction and directly strengthens customer loyalty. Customer satisfaction is expected to transmit part of the influence of service quality to loyalty, while customer trust is proposed to influence the strength of the relationship between service quality and loyalty. The framework is situated within Nigeria's digital financial services environment, where commercial banks, mobile applications, internet banking platforms, automated payment channels and digital financial service providers compete for customer retention. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design and structural equation modelling are proposed for subsequent empirical validation. Five tables present the construct definitions, hypothesised relationships, measurement indicators, proposed analytical procedures and a model for reporting empirical findings. The article contributes an integrated framework for understanding how technological performance, customer evaluations and confidence in financial institutions may jointly explain loyalty in Nigerian digital banking. Its propositions require validation with primary data before empirical conclusions can be drawn.

detail.abstract:
Purpose – Ten years after Barger et al. (2016) reviewed consumer engagement on social media, this paper revisits how engagement is measured. It reviews and integrates language-based measures of engagement, develops a conceptual framework, and proposes a research agenda.

Design/methodology/approach – The paper reviews the marketing and adjacent literatures on measuring engagement from text, including natural language processing and large language model methods, organized by the cognitive, emotional, and behavioral dimensions of engagement and across both the consumer and the firm.

Findings – Engagement counts capture the act of engagement but not its content. Language-based methods can in principle recover the cognitive and emotional dimensions that the consumer brand engagement construct names but that behavioral counts do not reach. The paper maps the linguistic signals and measurement approaches available for each dimension on both sides of the consumer-firm dyad, separates what the literature supports from what remains to be done, and identifies the conversation, rather than the isolated post, as the unit at which the co-creative process becomes measurable.

Originality/value – The paper offers a framework that (1) distinguishes the engagement act from engagement content and positions language-based measurement as the means of recovering the latter, (2) extends to both parties of the consumer-firm dyad and locates the conversation as the unit of analysis, (3) states five testable propositions with boundary conditions, and (4) sets out a prioritized agenda for research.

Keywords – Social media engagement, consumer engagement, firm engagement, natural language processing, large language models, engagement measurement

Paper type – Conceptual paper

detail.abstract: We study constrained assortment optimization in two-sided markets, where a platform chooses which alternatives to show each side and a match requires mutual selection. A key difficulty is that a supplier's optimal revenue need not be submodular in its pool of interested customers. To address this, we develop a continuous multiple-knapsack framework based on γ-cover modularity, a generalization of submodularity. For normalized monotone γ-cover modular functions, we establish a correlation-gap bound of γ/(1-e-γ). We also develop a stochastic projected-gradient method for optimizing their multilinear extensions over compact convex feasible regions, achieving the factor (1-e-γ)/γ in expectation, up to an additive optimization error. The value function of an m-resource continuous multiple-knapsack problem is further shown to be m-cover modular, with a tight dependence on m. We apply this framework to customer-initiated two-sided assortment optimization under multinomial logit choice, with pair-dependent revenues and cardinality constraints that may restrict the customer (initiating) side, the supplier (responding) side, or both. Using a reference no-purchase parameter of suppliers and relaxing the display limit to an aggregate cardinality-load constraint that bounds the total fractional display, we construct a two-resource continuous multiple-knapsack surrogate that is 2-cover modular. Pointwise, the original terminal revenue lies between the surrogate value and twice that value. Combining this pointwise comparison with an LP relaxation and our correlation-gap bound yields polynomial-time randomized static policies with a (1-e-2)/4-ϵ approximation guarantee for both the responding-side and two-way constrained regimes. These guarantees hold against the customer-initiated adaptive optimum under the same display limits. Stronger guarantees hold when revenues depend only on the supplier or when display limits apply only to customers.

detail.abstract: In March 2025, Kenya's President and the country's most prominent opposition leader signed a ten-point memorandum that dissolved, in substance if not in name, the distinction between the governing coalition and the official opposition. This article asks what remains of the separation of powers once that distinction collapses: when the Leader of the Minority sits inside the government's own cooperation framework; when Parliament's oversight committees vote unanimously, across every party line, to protect a fund the courts have twice found unconstitutional; when two-thirds of the National Assembly can be found missing from the chamber at the precise moment a Finance Bill comes to its decisive vote; and when the Judiciary must negotiate its own survival budget with a Treasury it has no constitutional power to compel. Testing four provisions of the 2010 settlement (Articles 108, 118, 103 and 173) against the documented conduct of Kenya's Thirteenth Parliament between 2024 and 2026, the article argues that Kenya's constitutional architecture has not been abolished so much as choreographed: each institution performs its assigned steps, in the correct sequence, while the outcome is settled elsewhere. It closes by testing that finding against its strongest counter-evidence, courts and committees that still, on occasion, rule against executive convenience, before concluding that procedural fidelity and substantive capture are not, in Kenya's present arrangement, mutually exclusive.

detail.abstract: Psychologists increasingly use large language models (LLMs) as participants in experiments, sometimes to test process theories of how a manipulation influences a psychological state, the mediator, that in turn affects the decision-maker's behavioral response. Although researchers have begun to examine how the internal representations of LLMs influence their responses in behavioral simulations, there has been no systematic study of how psychological constructs are represented in LLMs and whether these representations influence the LLMs' responses in the way that process theories specify. We examined the representations of 66 constructs from 60 published experiments in 16 LLMs from different developers in a multitrait-multimethod design. Each construct had an identifiable representation that was stable across LLMs and across independently written descriptions of the construct. Following the causal chain from the manipulation through the mediator to the response, we further found that the manipulation's activation of the mediator's representation does not always lead to the response that the theory predicts: it does so most strongly when the activation occurs while the LLM processes the experiment's question, which directly precedes, and is thus closest in the causal chain to, the response. LLMs represent theorized psychological states, but their responses depend on these representations only partly.

detail.abstract: Accurate quantification of tail risk in multi-asset portfolios is critical for effective risk management and capital allocation, particularly during extreme market downturns. Traditional risk metrics such as Value at Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES) frequently underestimate downside risk when relying on the standard Gaussian copula, which fails to capture asymmetric tail dependence and extreme co-movements. This paper evaluates and compares the empirical performance of Clayton, Gumbel, and Student-t copulas against standard Gaussian copulas in measuring VaR and Expected Shortfall across diversified multiasset portfolios during systemic market crashes. Using daily return series across equity, fixed-income, and commodity classes, we estimate marginal distributions via GJR-GARCH models with standardized skewed Student-t innovations to isolate standardized residuals. Copula parameters are fitted using maximum pseudo-likelihood estimation, and portfolio tail losses are simulated via Monte Carlo methods. Our findings demonstrate that asymmetric copulas (Clayton and Gumbel) and fat-tailed elliptical structures (Student-t) substantially outperform Gaussian frameworks by capturing lower-tail dependence and joint tail heaviness. Specifically, the Student-t copula minimizes backtesting exceptions during crisis episodes, while the Clayton copula exhibits superior performance in capturing lower-tail contagion. Consequently, risk managers are advised to replace linear correlation assumptions with tail-sensitive copula specifications to avoid severe capital underestimation during financial panics.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This paper synthesizes a research program conducted with many collaborators over the past decade, and the intellectual debts are correspondingly deep: above all to Gordon L. Clark, with whom many of the framework’s components were co-developed, and to Carter Casady, Khaled Alsweilem, Adam Dixon, Alistair Barker, Soh Young In, Malan Rietveld, and many others whose collaborations shaped it. The fieldwork was made possible by the dozens of investment organizations that opened their doors to this research. Three specific disclosures are particularly appropriate. First, this paper builds directly on prior published work, in particular Reframing Finance (Monk, Sharma and Sinclair 2017), the investor-identity framework (Monk and Rook 2023) and the analysis of innovation constraints and catalysts (Monk, Rook, and Sharma 2026); elements of its argument appeared in compressed form in an opinion essay for fDi Intelligence, a Financial Times Group publication (Monk 2025). The present paper integrates those strands with a theory of role-model formation, transferability, and capital-flow effects. Second, the authors have served in advisory capacities with organizations discussed here, anonymized or named from the public record; those engagements are the source of some of the field evidence, and the dual role is a feature of the method as well as a limitation of it. Third, all case material has been anonymized, and no organization reviewed or approved this text. All errors or omissions are our own.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was funded by SLTI's long-term investor industry affiliate program.

detail.abstract:
Asset owner investors, such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, and endowments, often describe their investment approach in a peculiar vernacular: by naming the institutional role models that inspired it. References to the Yale Model, Canadian Model, Norway Model, Temasek Model, and, more recently, the Collaborative Model function as a kind of institutional shorthand, compressing organizational design, asset allocation, and portfolio implementation into a single label that communicates how a portfolio (and its performance) is meant to be produced. Yet the practices associated with a model cannot be understood independently of the organizational identity from which they emerged: its categorical advantages, cultivated advantages, challenges, and plans.

Drawing on a long-running qualitative research program and published accounts of canonical investment models, this paper examines what models encode, how they acquire role-model status, and why their adoption produces uneven results when transposed to other organizations. We argue that imitation often transfers visible practices without the complementary capabilities and enabling conditions on which those practices depend. Effective adaptation therefore requires joint consideration of organizational design, portfolio policy, and implementation, rather than treating the organization as a residual of an allocation decision. We also distinguish institution-specific exemplars from proto-models: organizing frameworks whose implementation must be specified by each adopter. The paper develops an account of model formation and diffusion, identifies mechanisms through which these processes may influence capital flows, and offers practical disciplines for identity assessment and the evaluation of transferability.

detail.abstract: Occupational licensing is commonly measured at the state level, although authorization requirements also appear in local codes. We assemble 39,600 jurisdiction-category records from 2,593 jurisdictions covering 1,074 occupations and regulated activities and construct county measures of licensing breadth and conditional intensity in 2025. Both vary within states and are nearly uncorrelated. The positive relationship between intensity and workplace employment in the raw county cross section disappears after adjustment. Across 214 state-border pairs, a one-standard-deviation increase in intensity is associated with 1.40 fewer workplace jobs per 100 residents. The corresponding resident-employment and industry-aligned estimates are imprecise.

detail.abstract: An AI service provider sells more than access to a model. It chooses a service promise, the information used to verify that promise, and an interface that customers may find costly to replace. We study these choices by extending the spatial contracting framework of Townsend and Zhorin. A Prescott-Townsend lottery program supplies observed-and hidden-effort surplus frontiers; a separate power-law specification yields three candidate market regimes as adaptation costs change: direct competition, protected hinterlands, and local monopoly. In a sequential contract-offer game, a challenger can respond to the incumbent's published promise and may gain from moving second. We then establish an incumbent-selection result. An informed incumbent retaining its least costly workloads leaves a higher-cost pool for a challenger, lowering the challenger's pooled contracting frontier and, under explicit restrictions, potentially making entry infeasible. The application distinguishes customer service value, the agent's optimization reward, and the designer's target outcome. A conditional target-value proposition and a KL-regularized logit representation show why greater measured performance or easier switching need not have a uniform welfare effect. The model identifies how a shift in contracting feasibility can overturn the advantage conferred by offer timing, and specifies the conditions under which these effects can be compared.

detail.abstract:
South Korea is actively spreading artificial intelligence (AI) transformation (AX) among its manufacturers, but the core supply base that drives it depends on foreign technology. Global competition has moved beyond individual technologies, the separate layers of the stack, to a contest of full-stack vertical integration for control of every layer of the stack, from energy to applications, and platform lock-in is entrenching the dominance of a handful of fi rms. In this setting, spreading AX without regard to the supply side could end in dependence on foreign platforms: a replay, on the AX stage, of Korea’s materials, parts, and equipment crisis.

This paper looks for a way through in what distinguishes the AI ecosystem from the AX ecosystem. The upper layers of the stack, which produce general-purpose intelligence, are a contest of capital and scale in which catching up is not realistic. By contrast, industry-specifi c AI (vertical AI), which implements that intelligence in industrial settings, and the capability to supply it are where Korea, with its accumulated manufacturing experience, can realistically compete. The paper analyzes four structural limitations of Big Tech’s focus on general-purpose AI and reviews developments in the major economies. It then proposes a response that moves beyond AX adoption toward stronger supply capability: pursuing demand and supply together and staking an early claim to operational standards.

detail.abstract: This paper extends the damped-sinc (DSINC) method for American options beyond the affine Heston class to general one-factor stochastic-volatility models. We show that the collapse identity, which reduces the early-exercise integral to a single spectral integral, remains valid for these models. Damping between zero and one is admissible whenever the discounted spot is a nonnegative local martingale. An Itô transformation of the volatility factorizes the conditional characteristic function and identifies a natural coordinate for approximating the exercise boundary. The 3/2 model admits closed-form joint transforms in terms of Kummer functions, while uncorrelated SABR admits a Bessel representation. When a practical closed-form transform is unavailable, the required volatility integral is computed directly by solving one backward equation per frequency, without a grid in the log-price. Through a known change of volatility coordinate, this approach also accommodates correlated SABR. Tests on the 3/2, SABR, GARCH and lognormal-volatility models show agreement with fine finite-difference benchmarks to within one basis point of the strike. Computational cost is comparable to or lower than that of our finite-difference implementation, except for the slower Hankel implementation of uncorrelated SABR.

detail.abstract: Some public agricultural credit is meant to fund resilience investments such as irrigation, yet a capital-constrained farmer can spend it on current production. We compare two interest-free government loans: a flexible operating loan usable for any purpose up to a cap, and an earmarked resilience loan equal to the project's cost, which the farmer may divert to production. The farmer borrows any remaining funds from a competitive bank whose rate rises with default risk. The government chooses monitoring intensity to minimize its expected fiscal burden from disasters, public-loan losses, and monitoring expenditure; detection redirects funds to the project without imposing costs beyond compliance. The flexible loan always raises the farmer's payoff relative to bank financing, yet a larger cap can crowd out resilience investment. While both investment choices require bank borrowing, each additional public dollar replaces bank debt and is worth more under noninvestment because the interest-free public loan is repaid less often. At larger caps, credit can expand production under noninvestment with diminishing gains while still replacing bank debt under investment, allowing the financing advantage to shift toward resilience. When public borrowing is matched across the two programs for each investment choice and other financing terms are unchanged, restricting use never lowers resilience, the chance that the project is built. The earmarked loan, however, is sized to the project: it can exceed a small flexible loan, leaving more credit to divert, or fall short of a generous one, which funds production as well as the project. Either way, diversion can pay where flexible credit would induce investment, and monitoring that catches only some diversion then leaves less resilience than flexible credit. Both farmer and government gain from earmarking only when the flexible cap is below the project's cost and earmarking restores resilience that flexible credit fails to induce. Our analysis suggests judging public credit by the resilience it induces and the fiscal burden it leaves, not by loan volume or formal earmarking.

detail.abstract:
This study analyzes two decades of South Korean vehicle sales data by fuel type to trace structural change in the domestic automobile market, and uses these findings to compare the policy stances of the two ministries spearheading the shift to electric vehicles.

Measured by total sales, the domestic market has reached a mature, stable stage, but its composition by fuel type is being reshaped rapidly. The market share of internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles plunged from 89.9 percent in 2020 to 57.4 percent in 2025, while the shares of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) and electric vehicles (EVs) expanded sharply, to 28.5 percent and 14.1 percent, respectively.

Within the same market, the three vehicle segments are thus at different stages of their life cycles: maturity and decline, transitional growth, and early diffusion. The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment (MCEE) and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources (MOTIR), which lead electrification policy, agree on the direction of the transition but diff er in their policy instruments and in how they view HEVs.

The MCEE builds its approach around demand-pull policies and treats a complete shift to zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) as the ultimate goal, whereas MOTIR favors a gradual transition of the supply-side ecosystem, including support for parts makers, and accepts HEVs as a bridging technology.

Building on this analysis, the study sets out three policy tasks: designing differentiated policies that reflect the different life-cycle stages of the three vehicle segments, formally adopting a cross-ministerial transition timeline grounded in long-term transition scenarios, and aligning the timing of demand-side deployment targets with supply-side support to help parts makers transition to electrification.

detail.abstract: Leader development has long asked leaders to name their values, and far less how a value, once held, becomes the person a leader is. This working paper sets out the Values-to-Destiny Sequence, a practice-derived model of leader identity formation in nine steps: values, culture, belief systems, mindset, language, actions, habits, character, and destiny. The Sequence extends a popular chain from thoughts to destiny by beginning with values and by naming the environment a value builds, the beliefs and mindset that environment forms, and the language through which mindset becomes action. The paper relates each link to established research, rates the strength of that support, and organizes the Sequence into four dimensions of identity formation: Values Clarity, Culture & Belief Architecture, Language Alignment, and Character Formation. It sets out eight testable propositions, including the Upstream Principle, that character is changed most durably by working on the values upstream of it, each with the evidence that would count against it, a research design, and evidence-tagged implications for leader development. Destiny is treated as a long-run trajectory, not a measurable outcome; the paper proposes tests for selected links rather than for the endpoint. It is a conceptual, practice-based contribution, not an empirical study.

detail.abstract: This preprint presents a condensed synthesis of the main findings of a scoping review on multiagent systems and emerging agent-to-agent coordination in tourism and hospitality. The review identified 68 studies published between 1998 and 2026 and examined how computational agents have been used in travel planning, recommendation, tourist assistance, negotiation, visitor management, forecasting and service coordination. The results show technological change but also considerable continuity. Recent systems based on large language models extend task decomposition, specialised roles, critique and response review, while many of the underlying coordination problems were already present in earlier multi-agent architectures. The evidence also shows that the presence of several agents should not be interpreted as evidence of interoperability or autonomous ecosystem operation. Most studies continue to evaluate prototypes, components, simulations or bounded computational tasks, with limited evidence of sustained operation across independent tourism organisations. The findings suggest that the more relevant transition is not from one generation of artificial intelligence to another, but from coordination within relatively closed systems towards agent interaction across services, platforms and organisational boundaries. This transition makes governance, authorisation, traceability, human supervision and failure recovery part of the technical and organisational architecture of future agent-to-agent tourism ecosystems.

detail.abstract: Culturally charged product labels can shape market valuations and liquidity without altering physical attributes. We examine Hong Kong housing, where in Cantonese 4 sounds like "death" and 8 like "prosperity." Using 141,386 first-hand apartment transactions at market prices during 1996-2018, we estimate causal effects of floor labels with two complementary approaches. First, we compare each unit with identically configured units on neighboring floors in the same vertical stack, identifying label effects as jumps at floors ending in 4 or 8 against a smooth floor-price trend. We find that units on floors ending in 4 sell for 2% less and take five weeks longer to transact, whereas those ending in 8 command a 0.85% premium and sell a week faster. During financial crises, superstition discounts and premia widen, suggesting that economic stress heightens consumers' reliance on heuristics in consequential decisions. Second, we exploit variation across buildings in developers' omission of unlucky floor numbers to isolate the label's effect from that of physical height, confirming that the effects are entirely labeldriven. To distinguish buyers' own preferences from resale speculation, we examine fixed-price, resale-restricted public housing and find that buyers choose unlucky floors later and lucky floors earlier in balloted allocation queues.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether competition law can govern an economy soundly when efficiency, equity and sustainability pull in different directions. Kenya and South Africa present a mirror image. Kenya's Constitution of 2010 carries a dense architecture of economic values, but its Competition Act speaks the language of consumer welfare and its enforcement favours settlement over doctrine. South Africa's Competition Act pursues transformation openly, but the public interest inquiry floats free of any principled limit and leans on ministerial discretion. The argument is that each system suffers a distinct pathology: under-constitutionalisation in Nairobi, overinstrumentalization in Pretoria. Tested against Walmart/Massmart, the Burger King merger, section 29(8) of the Kenyan Act, the Canal+/MultiChoice conditions and the media platforms inquiry, the two pathologies explain outcomes that conventional analysis treats as unrelated. The paper then constructs the Proportionate Market Order test, a five-stage framework that converts constitutional values into reasoned, reviewable and time-limited competition decisions. The framework ranks no value above another. It disciplines how each is traded against the others, using the proportionality that both constitutions already demand for every limitation of a right. Fresh enforcement data, macroeconomic indicators and pending reform in both jurisdictions show why the matter is urgent. Eight recommendations follow.

detail.abstract: Plan-based services connect two decisions: whether and which plan to choose upfront, and how to use the service on individual occasions. How closely do customer preferences correspond across these decisions, and what does each reveal about plan demand? We develop a Horizon-Shared Preference (HSP) framework to estimate cross-horizon preference correspondence and evaluate its implications for plan-demand prediction. A complementary matched-information analysis examines the incremental predictive value of usage and plan-choice observations for the same plan-demand outcomes. We apply the approach to a stated-choice experiment on Mobility-as-a-Service in Hong Kong, in which 1,112 respondents each complete six plan-choice and six usage-choice tasks. We find that a preference component anchored by monetary-cost sensitivity exhibits positive but limited correspondence across decisions; imposing complete sharing substantially worsens model fit and plan-demand prediction. A second preference component, associated with plan value, is expressed more strongly in commitment decisions. Plan-choice observations also substantially improve demand prediction and the identification of repeated plan choosers within a fixed-size marketing list, even when customer profiles already include usage choices. The findings connect cross-horizon preference correspondence with the use of commitment and usage information in plan-demand assessment and customer prioritization.

detail.abstract:
When an AI model says gold will rise, a reader can score the call at the close but usually cannot check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and a trading season is one path through the market. I propose a standard of numbered requirements for measuring AI forecasts of financial markets and document its reference implementation, the open league AI Council · Markets, run by PolyHelper, with a published status per requirement. Fourteen large language models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, answer the same question on a shared price snapshot, each with its own account. Eleven of them forecast twelve indicators at four horizons before each New York open. Each counted answer is sealed into a SHA-256 hash chain before its reference price and anchored in Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps. From 21 October 2026 the counted run is declared in advance, and independent RFC 3161 authorities sign every stamped record, which also enters the Sigstore Rekor transparency log. On that first counted morning every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open, eight of them 29 minutes before it. The Brier score of the event asked is set against a 50% benchmark, the climatological base rate and prediction-market prices, and agreement is reported as a count of independent voices. On the development mornings of 19 and 20 October the models' probability pictures were as alike as those of about 1.6 independent forecasters. On 20 October three of the four closest pairs joined a US and a Chinese laboratory. Against a dated map of 23 AI forecasting and trading efforts, the league is the first live AI league on financial indicators to combine these elements. It is also the first AI market arena where seven US and seven Chinese models trade under one protocol beside readers assigned once, at random, to forecast before or after seeing the models. Thirty dated predictions, registered on OSF before posting, are scored in dated revisions.

detail.abstract: Spare parts providers commit to fill rate targets in Service Level Agreements (SLAs), which are evaluated over a finite horizon. Current practice plans inventories with long-run fill rate targets, which are easy to manage but do not control how often an SLA is met. We instead require the weighted average fill rate of a segment to reach the target with a prescribed probability within the horizon, and compare the inventory cost of this aggregate probabilistic target to long-run and item-level targets under different weightings. We introduce a Markov chain formulation for the finite-horizon fill rate distribution of an (R, s, Q) policy under intermittent demand and a scalable Lagrangian optimization algorithm for aggregate chance constraints. On a dataset of about 70,000 spare parts, item-level probabilistic targets raise inventory costs by up to 49% relative to the long-run status quo, whereas aggregate probabilistic targets, which pool service outcomes across items, cost at most 5.3% more. Our algorithm improves on the company's benchmark by up to 1.7%. Out-of-sample achievement rates fall at most 1.6 pp short of the prescribed probability for a 90% service target. Managers can thus commit to SLAs at the segment level with controlled risk at little extra cost.

detail.abstract: Migrating legacy enterprise applications to cloud-native data platforms requires decisions about application structure, data authority, transaction boundaries, and operational responsibility. Infrastructure relocation or container adoption alone does not establish that the resulting platform supports reliable enterprise work. This structured narrative review synthesizes research on cloud migration, microservice transition, distributed databases, analytical platforms, integration, and governance. Its objective is to compare architectural strategies and identify the evidence needed to select and sequence them. The synthesis distinguishes infrastructure rehosting, platform substitution, selective application decomposition, and analytical separation as overlapping options with different change boundaries. Their suitability depends on existing coupling, data semantics, operating capability, and the required transition period. Particular attention is given to coexistence between old and new environments, where synchronization, conflicting writes, access differences, and rollback assumptions can create risks absent from either endpoint considered alone. An original, unvalidated migration qualification framework is proposed that connects capability definition, dependency and state mapping, strategy selection, bounded transition, and operational acceptance. The contribution is a joint treatment of application boundaries and data authority, supported by a comparative decision matrix and prospective evaluation agenda. Assessment should examine meaningful output correctness, service behavior, recovery, authorized access, and sustained operating effort. No migration experiment, benchmark, performance gain, or empirically validated framework is claimed.

detail.abstract: Manufacturing equipment does not require one universal maintenance policy. Corrective, scheduled preventive, condition-based and predictive approaches differ in their cost, information needs, intervention burden and ability to control consequential failure. Choosing among them is a multiple-criteria decision problem, yet a simple weighted ranking can suggest an unsafe or infeasible option and can hide sensitivity to disputed weights. This conceptual paper develops a staged framework for selecting maintenance strategies for defined asset groups within a manufacturing system. A focused, non-exhaustive synthesis of maintenance policy and decision-analysis research informs a procedure that first defines functions and failure modes, then screens out alternatives that breach safety, technical or resource constraints. Eligible policies are evaluated on distinct criteria for safety and environmental exposure, availability, lifecycle cost, quality, implementation readiness and operational flexibility. A transparent weighting and outranking or distance-based comparison can support deliberation, while sensitivity and scenario analysis test whether the preferred policy survives plausible changes in assumptions. A second portfolio stage checks interactions among assets, outage windows, labour and spare-parts budgets. Three tables and two original diagrams translate the framework into a reviewable decision process. No plant data, numerical ranking or empirical improvement is claimed. The paper contributes a decision architecture that separates eligibility, preference and portfolio feasibility and specifies how future manufacturing case studies should test its usefulness against current policy selection practice.

detail.abstract: Enterprise artificial intelligence and predictive analytics require data architectures that support growing workloads without losing the consistency, traceability, and operational controls needed for dependable decisions. Cloud elasticity expands infrastructure choices, but infrastructure capacity alone does not establish data suitability or sustained predictive performance. This structured narrative review synthesizes research on cloud platforms, analytical storage, stream processing, production machine learning, data governance, and risk management. Its objective is to connect architectural scalability with the information and operational requirements of enterprise predictive services. Four themes organize the analysis: selecting workload boundaries, preserving temporal and semantic consistency, governing reusable data and model artifacts, and evaluating service behavior throughout operation. The synthesis distinguishes storage consolidation from information consistency, distributed processing from unlimited scalability, and reproducible pipelines from valid predictive evaluation. An original, unvalidated Enterprise Predictive Data Architecture Framework is proposed. It connects business decision requirements to governed data representations, workload-specific processing paths, model lifecycle controls, and continuing evidence of suitability. The contribution is a common assessment structure for comparing architectural choices without assuming that a lakehouse, warehouse, or streaming platform is universally preferable. The framework offers propositions for prospective evaluation rather than measured performance gains. Future studies should compare freshness, reproducibility, predictive validity, access correctness, and total operating effort under equivalent workloads and clearly stated service requirements.

detail.abstract: Engineering projects face cost and schedule deviations that can become difficult to reverse before conventional reports prompt action. Earned value management (EVM) measures performance against a scope-linked baseline, yet cost and schedule indices alone do not explain the causes of deviation or quantify future risk. This paper proposes a conceptual early-warning framework that integrates EVM, earned schedule, a maintained risk register and probabilistic forecasts. A focused synthesis of project-control studies informs five connected stages: baseline and progress assurance, performance signal generation, risk-event updating, joint cost and schedule scenario analysis, and escalation with documented action. The framework distinguishes an observed variance from an uncertain future outcome, separates approved scope changes from performance deterioration, and treats schedule exposure through network criticality rather than assuming that a monetary schedule variance measures time. Three tables define the data interfaces, trigger logic and governance responsibilities. Two reproduced figures from a peer-reviewed engineering project study, reused under its Creative Commons Attribution licence, illustrate the difference between a point cost forecast and a probability distribution and show how forecast intervals change over successive reporting periods; they are external published findings, not results of this paper. The paper contributes a testable decision architecture rather than claiming a validated improvement. Future evaluation should compare warning lead time, forecast calibration, false alarms and action outcomes against standard EVM and riskregister practices in real engineering projects.

detail.abstract: The study, examined the uses of the major resources over which conflicts arise within floodplain, and explained how competing claims on land, water, pasture, and fishery resources translated into recurrent tension among resource-user groups. The aim was achieved through a mixed method adopted where 384 samples were analysed in survey, 28 participants in FGD and twelve in KII. The findings were major resource use patterns identified arable land as the primary contested resource, and is used mainly for farming. Fishing resource vandalism was the most prevalent, while grazing on cultivated land, expanding farm sizes, and fishing and sailing within private farm boundaries drove most tensions and disputes. People perceived that all resources as abundant, though scarcity linked to high population density arose when demand exceeded supply with resources availability peaking between September and December amid a broader shift reflecting diminishing resources, population pressure, and socio-economic change. Land use and land cover data traced this trajectory in 1995 showed minimal human interference, 2005 marked modest land conversion, and by 2024 forest loss and cropland expansion had intensified. Resource competition was highest from September to December, it was minimal between 1995 and 1999, then intensified from January to April of which correlate with lower population size. This demographic shift caused irregular, unsustainable resource use. Boundary disputes were the most frequent and severe conflicts, indicating uneven resource distribution in the area. The study recommends seasonal adaptive governance, advocates for multidimensional strategy to include; sustainable resource development, capacity building, temporal and targeted conflict resolution, environmental conservation and user education.
